#3649. Grand Theft Auto 6: The Kotaku Review

GTA 6 is a game that at times feels almost embarrassingly expensive and extravagant. I cleaned a boat with a pressure washer and watched the suds build up realistically in the concrete below my characterâs flip-flops. I ran through a tram station and spotted over 100 different NPCs milling about, all unique and all moving. Hair gets wet. Sweat builds up on backs. Even for Rockstar, the master of tiny details, GTA 6 is overflowing with examples of what happens when you let a studio work on one game for a decade. Itâs a lot, but it all serves the purpose of creating a virtual world that players can truly get lost in.Â

Iâve put over 150 hours into GTA 6 on PlayStation 5 Pro, and I expect Iâll spend even more time in this digital recreation of Florida and Miami, as thereâs so much to do and see in Vice City. I doubt most players will see half of it. I bet I wonât ever see it all.Â

GTA 6 is a massive third-person open-world game, like Rockstarâs previous offerings. It merges the slower pace and slice-of-life mechanics from Red Dead Redemption 2 with the urban sprawl and crime-movie feel of GTA IV and GTA V. Itâs a more grounded journey than its predecessors, one which requires more planning and consideration if you want to survive and succeed as modern-day Bonnie and Clyde, robbing small stores as you work your way up to bigger scores, like banks. Itâs often a tougher game than any past GTA, but in a way that rewards skill and patience. Or bravery, stupidity, and luck.Â

I have quibbles about some clunky controls and some story pacing problems in the gameâs later chapters, but like crappy cupholders in a million-dollar supercar, they donât really get in the way of what’s here. Instead, they’re minor issues to point at as I hit the gas and go 200 MPH with the radio blasting.Â

The best part of Grand Theft Auto 6 isnât what I expected. It’s not the crime, or the action, or the massive world to explore, though all of those parts are excellent and better than ever. The real standout of GTA 6, the part of the game that kept me hooked and which I wonât forget anytime soon, is its central duo, Jason and Lucia.

Not only do they have very different motivations than past GTA protagonists, wanting to create a better life for themselves and escape their life of crime instead of vying to become crime lords or get revenge, but they are easily Rockstarâs most fully fleshed-out, believable, and relatable characters.

At the start of the game, Jason and Lucia are separated after a short relationship. Lucia tried to rob a payday loan place after breaking up with Jason and, in the process, got arrested. This moment has huge ramifications for both of their lives and ultimately pulls them together early on in GTA 6âs runtime.

Jason, an Army vet, is more reserved than your average GTA protagonist. Heâs a loyal man who’s conflicted about the things he does to get by and try to make things better for himself and Lucia. A lot of people tell Jason heâs a good guy, but heâs never sure if he really is. Meanwhile, Lucia, a petty thief living paycheck to paycheck, knows sheâs flawed and doesnât care nearly as much as Jason about that fact. Sheâs more focused on improving her life by any means and has a bigger goal that drives her to take bigger risks.Â

Together they balance each other out, with Jason often acting as a voice of reason and Lucia pushing him to strive for more. Their dynamic is unlike anything Iâve seen in a Rockstar-developed game, and thanks to some stellar writing and performances, I found myself deeply caring about these two criminals just trying to make it.Â

Throughout the entire run of GTA 6, Jason and Lucia interact as you would expect two real people who care for each other would. They joke with each other, comment on events happening around them, share secrets, and help each other when they can.Â

Spending time with them is never annoying. Neither Lucia nor Jason pesters the player when youâre hanging around with them in the open world. Sometimes they might point out that you missed a turn or a possible way to sneak into a gang-infested hideout. This never felt like some annoying video-gamey handholding, just a couple working together.Â

While Jason and Lucia are both skilled at stealing cars, shooting guns, and running around causing chaos, they arenât always treated as equals in the world. While playing as Lucia, I was hit on by random assholes and catcalled by men on the street. It wasnât constant, but it happened enough that it was impossible to ignore. Some characters will also doubt Luciaâs abilities, but never question Jasonâs skills as a murderous criminal. It adds an intriguing wrinkle to playing as either character. Lucia feels like she has to work harder to prove herself among her criminal peers. Jason often has her back in these scenarios, but lets her hold her own, and she does so with sharp words and strong punches.Â

Even outside of when they directly speak to each other to tell stories or give feedback, the other’s presence is always felt, sometimes in small gestures, like one holding the door for the other as they enter a building. And sometimes, depending on how you handle their relationship, through more intimate moments that either Jason or Lucia, regardless of whether the player is controlling them, can initiate when theyâre feeling ready to fool around.Â

One time while I was playing as Jason, after spending all day and most of the night with Lucia, we came home, and I couldnât even get through the door before both of them were on top of each other. If you were wondering: Jason and Lucia fuck a lot in this game, assuming you play them as a couple, which I did.Â

It didnât take long for me to fall in love with Jason and Lucia. And I spent the entire game rooting for them, even as their situation became more dangerous and desperate, largely due to factors outside of their control.Â

While Jason and Luciaâs relationship, be it platonic or romantic depending on your choices, never loses steam or feels like it stops evolving, GTA 6âs main overarching narrative of criminal conspiracy and mayhem does start to falter in the back half.

In a later chapter of the story, the momentum that had carried everything forward up until that point fades. It feels like GTA 6âs story begins spinning its wheels at this point. By the end, the narrative picks back up, and the stakes grow even larger as Jason and Lucia rely on themselves to take on the world. But even when the story started to lose steam, and I felt myself wondering how many more missions Iâd have to do before something big happened, Jason and Lucia were there to keep me going. Lucia doing an impersonation of Jasonâs deep voice always made me chuckle, as did any time Jason gave her crap about her bad driving after I crashed another car.Â

Just know there are multiple endings, and after seeing two of them in my time with the game, I can confirm that how you play and what choices you make can have a huge impact on how things turn out. Happy endings areâ¦not common in this line of work, but not impossible.Â

Even if the rest of GTA 6 didnât work, Jason, Lucia, and their relationship would still carry it across the finish line. Thankfully, the rest of Grand Theft Auto 6 is very good, too.Â

The second-best part of GTA 6, behind our Bonnie and Clyde duo, is the world of Leonida, the state that Vice City is located in. It is the most detailed, gorgeous, and alive open world Iâve ever experienced in a video game.Â

GTA 6 starts off in the southern part of the map, far away from the skyscrapers and glitz of Vice City. You can almost see it in the distance from the small coastal town where GTA 6 begins. Itâs the kind of scale Iâve not really felt before in an open-world game. And all that spaceâ¦it ainât empty.Â

It feels like every inch of GTA 6 is filled with life. With movement. Withâ¦something. Even areas like the huge swamp, which at first glance might seem empty, reveal themselves to be filled with detail and specificity. That swamp, for instance, is teeming with creatures, big and small. The wind rustles the leaves of every tree and plant around. Planes fly overhead at different altitudes. I ran deeper in and stumbled upon a giant snake with a dead body in its mouth. Later, I found a crashed plane smuggling drugs. In the distance, I spotted dark clouds forming and bursts of lightning. Rain was coming. And later, I watched a lightning bolt crash into the woods and start a small fire.Â

All this happened in the span of an hour in one relatively small section of the swamp, itself a small portion of the larger world. Itâs at times overwhelming. Driving through the city, which I didnât reach until nearly a dozen hours into the game, I felt guilty about all the life and detail I was speeding by at 100 MPH.Â

I was also much more focused on the road than in past GTA games. The streets in GTA 6 arenât as wide as those in GTA V, and there are far more cars on the road. Crashing into these other drivers can quickly damage your vehicle, making it harder to steer or accelerate. But I didnât find any of this annoying. Instead, it made it satisfying to weave through traffic to escape police. The act of just driving a car is so much more exciting than it’s ever been in the franchise. It felt like a real skill Iâd developed after a few hours and one which I always enjoyed using, making long road trips across the map feel less like a chore and more like an opportunity to explore more of the game.Â

All of these changes to driving and the roads in GTA 6 also forced me to sometimes slow down or stop, giving me more time to take in all the atmosphere and detail packed into the game.Â And I do recommend slowing down whenever possible and just soaking in Vice City and Leonida. GTA 6 is a game that truly rewards exploration and poking around. Even 150 hours in, Iâm still encountering new random events, side characters, and more.

One day in Vice City, as I was walking down the street, I entered a small convenience store to buy some food and boost my health stat. But inside, I found a criminal behind the cash register and a dead body on the floor near them. I held the left trigger to lock onto the robber, a young woman, and questioned her about what was happening. She said to mind my own business and leave. I taunted her next. This was a mistake. The young woman robbing the small store was armed with a gun and pointed it at me. I quickly drew my own pistol, and we started shooting. A second later, she was dead. I grabbed the cashâI mean, I couldnât just leave it there on the groundâand ran out the back where I found the robberâs car. In the trunk were drugs and ammo. Before I could look around more, I heard sirens. The cops were coming. I quickly hopped a fence and ran by some people who werenât happy that I was running through their backyard.Â

Just another day in Leonida. Iâve truly never experienced an open world like this before, and every time I think Iâve seen it all or canât be more impressed by it than I already am, Iâm quickly proven wrong.Â

One night, I climbed the gameâs tallest mountain, and when I reached the top, it was nighttime. Vice City and its sprawl were laid out in front of me, thousands of twinkling lights and bright dots floating in the darkness miles and miles away. Lucia took it in and exclaimed to Jason that it was gorgeous. He agreed. So did I.Â

But it ainât just a big pretty world with lots of moving parts. Itâs also Rockstarâs attempt to simulate as much of life in Leonida as possible. Youâll find over 600 stores to shop at, gyms to work out in, gun ranges to visit, golf courses to play on, zoos to explore, gas stations to rob, bars to chill in, animals to hunt, mod shops to improve cars at, and even working buses and trains with actual schedules and passengers.Â

You can, and I did, just live out a normal day in the life of Jason and Lucia, freely swapping between them to see what the other was up to at any time.Â

During one session as Jason, I hit the gym early in the morning, then hopped in my off-road car and headed north to do some hunting. When I wanted to shake things up, I swapped over to Lucia, and a few seconds later I was playing as her. She was chilling on a beach, and a friend of hersâthey each have their own social livesâtexted, checking in on me. I replied and then got hit on by a random asshole. So I taunted him until he called me a bitch and left. A moment later I swapped back to Jason, and he was at a nearby gas station with his gun out. I took the hint and hunted a different kind of animal, and came away $450 richer. Other times Iâd switch to find them watching TV, chatting up a random NPC, or driving around the city.Â

The incredibly realistic graphics and the focus on simulating not just the fact that your partnerâs life continues when you arenât near them, but that they exist in an entire living world, one where you can gain weight, get tired, and ride the bus, do at times clash with the parts of the game where Rockstar clearly didnât want to annoy people with the sorts of inconveniences that can emerge out of realism.Â

For example, every store in the game is open 24 hours a day. This means you can walk into a barber shop at 3 am and get a haircut. To the gameâs credit, the shop was empty besides the employees at that time, something I found true in other stores and locations at odd hours. But these bits of video gameâness stood out all the more because the world was otherwise so lifelike.

All this simulation, fancy visuals, and scale does have a cost. The game runs at 30FPS, even on PS5 Pro. And in some areas of the map, like on the packed streets of Vice City, I noticed framerate drops. I also spotted slowdown during large firefights with police. It never became unplayable, but it does make me curious to see how this game will look on a powerful PC.Â

If youâve reached this point and are starting to wonder if this is still a GTA game, donât worry; thereâs plenty of shooting, robbing, car theft, murder, and action to be had. But this time around, crime isnât as easy as it has been in the past, which makes it so much more rewarding and fun.Â

Police in GTA 6 are not to be underestimated. They can quickly overwhelm Lucia and Jason and will share important details about the couple with each other on the radio, making it harder to evade officers looking for you. It pays to keep a change of clothing in your trunk and store large weapons in there too, unless you want every cop in the area to come calling after people spot an armed person matching a suspected robberâs description.Â

Even hitting a small gas station is thrilling because of how much smarter police are and how much more challenging GTA 6 can be.

You can walk into a store, pull out a gun, kill the clerk, take his money, and run. But the surveillance camera will record you, people in the area will report your location, and cops will be after you quicker due to the murder and gunfire.Â

Instead, you should sneak in through the back, put on a mask, destroy any camera recordings, disable the alarm, crack open the safe, and then head out front to force the clerk to hand over the cash. Then bail, leaving him alive, and enter your car, which you smartly parked further away from the scene. Once you reach a safe spot, you can change your clothes if you have any heat, and then drive by the cops rushing to the scene without any of them suspecting a thing.Â

Pulling off perfect crimes like that, even on a small scale, is so rewarding.Â

Even the simple act of stealing a car in GTA 6 is more engaging and fun than it’s ever been in past games. Some cars are easy to just pop the lock on, hop in, and hotwire. But other cars demand you use a slim jim to shimmy open the lock via a simple, quick mini-game. And still other, fancier cars require Jason and Lucia to use a key cloner to gain access, which is also pulled off via a mini-game. Those cars canât even be hotwired, meaning for a large chunk of the game you have to avoid the coolest cars in Vice City and settle for rust buckets and unlocked sedans. And even some of those cars have trackers that make it easier for police to find you later, and harder to modify and sell them to shops around the city.Â

But like the slimmer roadways and more punishing crashes, this change to the GTA formula didnât frustrate me. On the contrary, I found it so much more exciting to steal cars in GTA 6. I became skilled at spotting cars that would likely be easier to steal than others without needing to use the car-scanning app included on your in-game phone. (Thereâs also an Instagram-like social media app on there, and you can text and call other characters, including your partner.)Â

And if you just canât help yourself, well, you can always steal any car driving around the map by yanking its driver out if you really want that badass Banshee. Jason and Lucia can also drive boats, planes, helicopters, dirt bikes, semi-trucks, airboats, buses, bulldozers, jet skis, andâif youâre brave enough to enter the gameâs military baseâeven a jet or tank. Good luck with that.Â

"Welcome to Vice City. Enjoy spending your next few years exploring every inch of this place!"

Third-person open-world action game with two playable characters and some RPG-like systems, cover-based shooting, and lots of customization options.

Jason and Lucia, the open world, challenging police, skillful driving, mission variety, multiple endings, and the music.

Some clunky controls, performance issues in big fights, and a back half that loses some narrative oomph.

152 hours. Finished main story campaign, saw two different endings, tried out most side activities, completed most side missions, and explored nearly the entire map.

Gunplay, like other parts of the GTA formula, is also more challenging, but better, than ever in GTA 6. Thatâs largely because Rockstar has moved away from the easy auto-aim nonsense of GTA V. Now, combat plays out more like it did in Max Payne 3, with a focus on manual aiming and landing headshots or, if you want to avoid killing people and being labeled a psycho by the in-game criminal profile system, shooting people in the kneecaps. (That profile system can change how characters react and how aggressive police will be when chasing you down.)Â

Guns also feel louder and more powerful. When a robbery goes wrong and bullets start flying, it’s scary and tense, and I always wanted to get out of there as soon as possible. You canât take too much damage before it becomes a problem, so shootouts are risky, but not impossible, to survive. Sometimes, Iâd just wing a cop or gang member in the arm, and theyâd realistically fall back, giving me enough time to slip away before they got back up and started shooting again.Â

Alongside all these moving parts and systems, a classic Rockstar problem is back in GTA 6: clunky controls.Â

Sometimes Iâd want to loot a body, but instead Jason would try to enter a nearby car. Other times Iâd want to reload my weapon, but Iâd kick someone instead. Getting objects out of trunks can be a real pain in the ass as context-sensitive button prompts appear and disappear based on where your character is looking.

I also occasionally found the controls a bit hard to keep straight. Every button on the gamepad does something; oftentimes, multiple actions are mapped to one button or a submenu. I still sometimes forget which d-pad button to hold to swap between Lucia and Jason during the heat of combat.Â

Still, anytime I had issues with the story or some clunky controls, Iâd turn a corner and discover a whole new section of this incredibly detailed world, quickly forgetting about those minor issues. As I said, crappy cup holders donât make a Bugatti any less fun to drive or impressive to sit in. And like those hyper-expensive and perfectly tuned supercars, GTA 6 feels like it was crafted by masters who’ve been making these kinds of open-world games for a long time and are better at it than any other studio by a very wide margin.Â

Adding to the feeling that Grand Theft Auto 6 is a masterclass in open-world game design are the missions. Yes, there are still the classic GTA missions that have you driving somewhere, shooting or stealing stuff, and then driving back to wrap it up. But so many missions in GTA 6 are very different from that usual formula.

A very early mission doesnât even involve guns or crime. Instead, Jason and his buddy Cal just clean up the living room, move a TV, get high, drink beer, and play video games together. We learn a lot about these two and how they care for each other in that moment, and nary a gun was fired or a murder committed.Â

But there are still plenty of big action-packed missions, and these, too, offer up experiences that arenât the usual GTA fare. A later mission involving a heist that spins out of control had my heart racing as the tension ramped up, and when all hell broke loose, GTA 6âs incredible world and improved combat were on full display.Â

Another mission involved a massive shootout that started on the street and worked its way through a building and onto a highway. During that whole fight, I was able to find my own way up, and when the game asked me to escape, I was free to do so in any car I wanted.Â

Thereâs a lot more flexibility in GTA 6âs missions, too. At one point, I was told to chase down a drug runner in a boat. The game asked me to hop on a dirt bike and follow it via a service road. Instead, I hopped into a small speedboat and the game justâ¦ rolled on, even commenting on my change of plans and changing up the objective on the fly. The person I was chasing even seemed to have different voice lines based on my choice.Â

GTA 6 is constantly reacting to your choices and actions, both in missions and when just out in the open world. It makes everything you do feel more meaningful and important, and it makes GTA 6 feel less restrictive than GTA IV and GTA V.Â

I also appreciated how experimental and creative GTA 6 can be in some of its missions. During one mission, Jason gets drugged and has to fight off tons of armed thugs. But as you run around and shoot, the world and the lights in it pulse with the music. Another mission involves Jason and Lucia robbing a bunch of tiny stores, and this is presented as a playable montage that hops from moment to moment seamlessly as a classic rock song that Rockstarâs embargo forbids me from naming plays in the background.Â

The licensed soundtrack is incredible, with a massive list of music across the gameâs various radio stations. And this time around, you can also listen to multiple in-game podcasts, either in your car or on foot via headphones. One is a true-crime podcast hosted by two terrible people that includes an episode dedicated to the serial killer side character in GTA IV.Â

Just like in past GTA games, thereâs a ton of content to watch on the TV, too, including multiple episodes of animated TV shows parodying American culture, politics, and police. Thereâs also a game show about people identifying men by looking at just their penises. Some of these shows advertise in the world or on social media, too. And characters will talk about shows and other parts of the world and post about them as the game goes on. Itâs just one more thing that makes the world of Vice City feel less like a static playground and more like a real place that reacts to my actions and crimes.

During one random event, I encountered a polar bear being transported to a zoo. I helped some protestors stop the truck, and the bear escaped, killing a few people and then running off in the city. Later, I saw a news article and a social media post about the bear. Another time I saw a viral clip of a stuntman doing a backflip at a football game and ripping open his suit to reveal his penis. Later on, I met that guy selling a cryptocoin and helped him out before he screwed me and some investors over, leading to news stories and social media posts from the tech company and its angry customers. And then a radio broadcast summed all this up via a short news piece while I was driving around later. This kind of stuff happens all the time in GTA 6, and it makes the whole world feel so alive and reactive.Â

This is the kind of stuff that elevates Rockstarâs open world above so many others. Sure, others might look good and feature fun missions. But Rockstarâs games are still the best at playing with the player and reacting to them. And GTA 6 takes this to a whole different level.

I also must shout out GTA 6âs original score, composed by Justice. Their soundtrack is a wild and wonderful mix of electronic dance, â80s funk, and rock guitars that permeates the game and adds so much to it. Strange moments are made weirder by their music. Silly moments are made even sillier and heartbreaking moments more painful.Â Iâll be jamming out to the gameâs score for weeks, I suspect. Even if you donât end up liking GTA 6 or even playing it, Justiceâs soundtrack is worth checking out.Â

A complete review of Grand Theft Auto 6 feels both impossible and in some ways unnecessary. For folks who see reviews as simply text that tells them if a game is worth buying or not, well, this is a game that doesnât need any help convincing people to buy it. And a game of this scale is hard to distill and evaluate, even with thousands of words. I sit here and feel like Iâve left out so much of what GTA 6 is.Â

Grand Theft Auto 6 is not the kind of game we get very often. Itâs a massive experience that is filled with more content and more ideas than some entire game franchises.Â

I had high expectations for Grand Theft Auto 6. This much time and money being poured into one video game leads to a lot of hype. Yet GTA 6 surprised me by not just meeting those expectations, but often exceeding them.Â

Jason and Lucia feel like a real couple and I loved rooting for them as they tried to escape the shitty hand they’d been dealt. The world is not just massive but also reactive, and feels the closest a video game has ever gotten to truly recreating all the vibes, life, and details youâd expect from a real place. The action is better than ever, but GTA 6âs quiet moments are really where the game leapfrogs over anything seen in a past GTA entry. And it all comes together to deliver something that truly makes the long wait feel both worth it and absolutely necessary.Â

There were nights when Iâd stay up far too late playing this game, not because I was crunching to finish it before the review embargo, but because I just didnât want to put the controller down.Â

GTA 6 is a truly remarkable game. A masterpiece of open-world design that brings forward the best parts of all of Rockstarâs past games into one billion-dollar adventure that is unlike anything Iâve played before. Itâs a game Iâll be playing for years, and I canât wait to talk about it with others.Â

#3648. Firaxis reportedly cuts a third of its staff as studio head departs and new XCOM struggles

Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games has laid off around 60 people.

The cuts, which took place today, account for about a third of the studio’s staff, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter. Studio head Heather Hazen is also leaving.

Its sources say Firaxis' unannounced XCOM game has faced development struggles and missed "a significant milestone over the summer". The project will continue, but "may face a shakeup as a result of the cuts".

A spokesperson for 2K, the Take-Two label that runs Firaxis, confirmed Hazen's departure to Bloomberg, and said the studio is "restructuring and recentering around the studio's core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years".

"As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis," the spokesperson continued. "These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis."

The layoffs come two days before the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, which is developed and published by Rockstar, a separate label at Take-Two.

In September, around 18 months after Civ 7's widely criticised launch - and as the legendary 4X series celebrates its 35th anniversary - Firaxis unveiled a host of new updates coming to the game as it continued to improve it. These included an atomic age update, dragging Civ 7 into the present and beyond, as well as its first paid expansion, Earthrise, both arriving next year.

Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick admitted earlier this year that the studio "got it wrong with Civ 7".

"The game is a really good game. And it's certainly a profitable enterprise for us. But this is one where I think what we tried to do was a bridge too far, from the consumer's perspective," he told Game File in May.

It’s not the first round of cuts at the studio - 2K confirmed an unspecified number of layoffs at Firaxis in September 2025, and around 30 jobs went in 2023.

#3647. Los Javis Are “Living a Dream” As La Bola Negra with Penélope Cruz, Guitarricadelafuente, and Miguel Bernardeau Collects Honors

While La Bola Negra continues to amass various accolades and early awards, like the Best Director award at this year's Cannes Film Festival and the Audience Award at the Toronto International Film Festival, directors Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo are extra grateful and overwhelmed by the film's reception and success in their home country of Spain.

Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

“You can't plan the miracle,” Calvo said during a panel conversation moderated by Ricky Martin at the inaugural Vanity Fair Screening Room at LACMA on Friday. “We’ve done many projects and each one of them has, they've all been good, but you never know when it's going to happen. And with La Bola Negra, we thought it was a very specific story and we thought that our audience was going to like it, but we never knew it was going to hit everyone. I think it's about to become the second highest grossing movie in the history of Spain. For me, the most beautiful part of it is the videos of the people hugging after the screenings, giving tissues to each other, comforting each other.”

La Bola Negra follows several gay men whose lives are bound together by their identities, love and loss, and the looming presence of the Spanish Civil War. The acclaimed Spanish language drama spans nearly a century and stars Miguel Bernardeau, Álvaro Lafuente Calvo (the singer known as Guitarricadelafuente) in his first major acting role, Carlos Gonzalez, Milo Quifes and Penélope Cruz.

Guitarricadelafuente at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

Following an exclusive screening of the film on Friday, Martin moderated a panel conversation featuring directors Ambrossi and Calvo, and stars Cruz, Guitarricadelafuente and Bernardeau. Calvo said they are all riding high on the positive audience reactions and reception. “Creating this sense of community and hearing people saying, ‘This movie changed me. It really made me understand things about me.’ The power that art has, we forget it, but then this happens and … the rest is a dream. The rest we're living is a dream.”

The directors also consider having Cruz play a small but pivotal role in the film to be part of their living a dream. When Martin asked Cruz how her longstanding allyship to the LGBTQ+ community shaped her intention or performance, she said, “I don't even ask myself that question because it's such a part of me, of the way that I was raised. My very young parents, my parents had me when they were 21. It was a house where the values were about respect and it was just like breathing. They didn't even have to sit us down and give us a lecture about it, it was the way my family was living by example. And on top of that, then I had my other master Pedro Almodóvar who I've worked with for seven movies. And I always remember growing up thinking, why is he not the president of our country? Because he was huge in a time where his presence was really necessary, not only through his films, but also by the things that he was saying. So I feel like all of that has shaped me.”

Miguel Bernardeau, Guitarricadelafuente, Penélope Cruz, Javier Calvo, Javier Ambrossi and Ricky Martin at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

She continued: “So when I have in my hands the possibility of playing somebody like Nené Romero, that is a reminder that unfortunately not everyone in the world feels the way we feel about everyone having a right for respect, everyone having a right to be themselves.”

Ricky Martin at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

For Martin, a Bola Negra superfan who admitted he was nervous to be asking questions instead of answering them, the actor and musician said he found out about his hosting opportunity only the day before and despite the nerves couldn't pass up the opportunity to help celebrate the film.

“I usually answer the questions, I never ask the questions, but I needed to be here,” he told the audience. “I saw this film and for a while I was in the movie. I was really touched. The acting, the way it was written, people are crying because that's just the way it is, [really moving].”

Miguel Bernardeau at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

The inaugural edition of Vanity Fair’s Screening Room pairs this year’s most compelling films with a slate of programming that includes post-screening panels and conversations with actors and filmmakers. The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

Some spoilers for The Nights Before Christmas can be found in this piece.

Hallmark is no stranger to holiday time-loop movies — the 2023 time-loop film Round and Round was my absolute favorite that year — so they definitely know how to write an effective one. Just like Hallmark Christmas movies follow a perfect movie formula, time-loop flicks also have a tried-and-true formula. A character who is unhappy in life encounters some kind of magical being or object that sets up the time loop, which they’ll ultimately spend the rest of the film trying desperately to break the curse.

Such core elements are so ingrained in the genre that it can be hard to reinvent the time-loop wheel, but by some miracle, Hallmark managed to do just that. And it totally worked!

The Nights Before Christmas premiered on the 2026 TV schedule this weekend and instantly became one of my favorite Hallmark Christmas movies of 2026. A fun yuletide flick, it follows Marty (Tyler Hynes), who is stuck reliving Christmas Eve over and over again after making a holiday wish to have more time to pursue his interests and hobbies. Marty takes full advantage of the gift of time, using it to meet people and master all his hobbies, and he seems content to keep living the same day on repeat.

Well, that is, until he meets Chloe (Laci J. Mailey), whom he feels an instant connection with. As Marty continues to repeat Christmas Eve with Chloe, he starts to wonder what his life would be like if he made it to Christmas morning.

Unlike other time-loop films, The Nights Before Christmas doesn’t start on day one of Marty’s loop. Instead, we meet Marty in one of the hundreds, if not thousands, of Christmas Eves he’s managed to live through. This is in immediate deviation from the genre that has made finding out you're in a time loop and freaking out about it one of the main features of a character’s arc. He’s also not freaked out or bothered by the sudden change in how time progresses; if anything, he welcomes and loves it.

The realization that this wasn’t going to be a day-one time loop was one that shocked me as soon as it happened, but I was totally on board with it. Admittedly, I’m not the biggest fan of the genre, so getting to watch Marty exist in the loop and be happy with his new, repetitive life was a much-needed and refreshing change to the otherwise predictable genre.

My Favorite Hallmark Christmas Movie Is Getting A Sequel, And I Can’t Wait

The film continues to reinvent the wheel as it progresses. For starters, almost every time Marty explains to Chloe that he’s stuck in a time loop, she believes him. This is unheard of with these types of films, as most of the time the stuck character has to jump through extravagant hoops to get anyone to believe and help them. Perhaps it helps that Marty isn’t asking for Chloe’s help in getting unstuck or advice on how to survive said time loop; he simply wants to spend time with her.

TNBC also finds fun ways to show the same day over and over again without long, drawn-out scenes. There’s a particularly fun sequence towards the end of the film where Marty is shown to be an excellent driver in a terrible snowstorm, despite having previously claimed to hate driving. It’s then revealed that this isn’t the first time he’s driven in the terrible storm and that the previous attempts have ended in disaster.

In its final act, the holiday film also manages to reinvent the way the time loop is resolved. All too often in these types of movies, the main characters must come to some great epiphany in order to put a stop to the loop and revert to the real timeline. This usually involves searching inward and changing something about themselves, but that’s not what happens in Nights Before Christmas. Instead, Marty discovers that he wasn’t put in the time loop to help himself, but rather he was put there to help Chloe get the Christmas she’s come to love and expect: a day with her parents. Needless to say, a narrative like this is quite refreshing in this genre.

So, if you’re a fan of time loops and Christmas, then The Nights Before Christmas needs to go to the top of your holiday watch list. The film can be streamed now with an active Hallmark+ subscription, or viewers can catch it airing on Hallmark again on Friday, November 20th at 10 PM, after the latest Countdown to Christmas lineup premiere.

#3645. GTA 6 Won’t Get A 60 FPS Mode, Even On PS5 Pro, Because It’s ‘Not Powerful Enough’

30 FPSGrand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar Games

Earlier this month, Rockstar Games confirmed Grand Theft Auto 6 targets 30 FPS on all platforms, even PlayStation 5 Pro. Before that news was revealed, I asked Rockstar if GTA 6 could receive a 60 FPS or even a 40 FPS mode in the future. And it sounds like, at least on current gen, that won’t be happening.

When Rockstar revealed that GTA 6 would target 30 FPS on PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S, some players didn’t take it well. Many had hoped that Rockstar would, like so many other developers this console generation, offer some kind of performance mode. So for some, it was very sad news. But others held out hope that, perhaps in a post-launch update, Rockstar would add in a 60 FPS option or even a 40 FPS option for players enjoying the game on a 120hz TV.

However, Rockstar has confirmed with Kotaku that this isn’t going to happen, even on PS5 Pro. GTA 6 is just too much for these current consoles.

“Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination,” explained Technology Production Director Marc Chambers. “On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR). The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.”

I’ve played over 130 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6 on PS5 Pro, and I don’t think the game is worse off for being locked to a framerate of 30 FPS. I’m somewhat of a framerate snob, but the gameplay in GTA 6 works totally fine at 30 fps. And the visuals are truly stunning, and more than make up for the lower framerate.

I know some people might suggest Rockstar turn off ray tracing and other fancy features to offer a 60 FPS option, but it would really take away from what the studio has built. GTA 6 is one of the best-looking games I’ve ever seen and easily sports the best-looking open world I’ve explored in my life. And a lot of that is down to the incredible lighting and ray-tracing tech that can be found in so many different parts of the world. Campfires cast orange, flickering glows on faces. Fancy red sports cars reflect the sunlight, tinting my crappy white car as I drive by them. The lights of my car’s dash and fuel gauge reflect in the windshield of my pickup truck as I cruise around the woods in the dark. Stuff like that adds a lot to the world and the vibes. Removing it would take away so much.

Even if you turn those visual features off, the game is still massive and incredibly alive, with dozens of planes in the air at all times, huge amounts of traffic, and multiple NPCs filling every frame of the game. So I’m not convinced it would be able to hit 60 FPS even with ray-tracing turned off or scaled back.

And hey, if history is any indicator of the future, this is the worst version of GTA 6 we’ll ever play. The game will almost certainly get ported to PC in the near future and run at 60 FPS or more over there, assuming your rig can run it. Later ports on next-gen machines in the future are also likely coming and will probably feature improved framerate options and more. So if you really want a 60 FPS option in GTA 6, you could just wait. But personally, I’m loving the game even at 30 FPS.

#3644. The Game Awards 2026 nominees announced, and GTA 6 leads with eight nods before it's even out

The Game Awards 2026 nominees have been revealed, and Grand Theft Auto 6 leads the pack with eight nominations, two days before it even launches.

Rockstar's crime epic is up for Game of the Year, Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, Best Art Direction, Best Score and Music, Best Audio Design, and Best Action/Adventure Game. Its eighth nomination is Manni L. Perez's Best Performance nod for her role as Lucia, which is how we found out who plays her in the first place.

THE GAME AWARDS: 2026 Nominee Reveal! (Game of the Year) THE GAME AWARDS: 2026 Nominee Reveal!Watch on YouTube

For Game of the Year, GTA 6 is up against 007 First Light, Control Resonant, Phantom Blade Zero, Resident Evil Requiem, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Nintendo is the most-nominated publisher, with 12 nominations across its games, followed by Capcom with 11, and Annapurna Interactive and PlayStation with nine each.

The nominees were picked by a jury of more than 160 media and creator outlets, who may get advance or pre-release access to games - which explains how GTA 6 made the cut before launch. The winners will be revealed on Thursday, 10th December, at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. Fans can vote on The Game Awards' website until 6pm PT on 9th December.

This year's show will stream for free on more than 40 platforms, including YouTube, Twitch, Prime Video, and Steam. Last year's show drew an estimated 171 million livestreams, up 11 percent on 2024's 154 million.

Is the outlaw couple hot together? Or are they running on empty?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

In GTA 6 you've got a partner in crime, and it's quite a bit different than it was when you were pulling heists with Michael, Franklin, and Trevor in the last game. Jason and Lucia aren't just criminal associates, they're a couple, and their romantic relationship is a big part of the story.

Jason and Lucia can grow closer or more distant, depending on your actions, behavior, and choices. That goes for everything from story missions to random criminal acts to everyday interactions and activities. Here's how Jason and Lucia's romance works in GTA 6.

There are four levels to Jason and Lucia's relationship that can change depending on how you play and the choices you make, one being the lowest and four being the highest. Here are the levels:

When you begin playing as a couple in Chapter 1, your relationship is already a strong one, though it'll still take a while to get it up to 4/4, if that's your goal. Certain actions, activities, and choices will raise your relationship score, and you'll know you've done it when you hear a chime and see a +♥️ appear on the right side of your screen.

Here are just a few actions that will add a ♥️ to your score, and there are plenty more:

*Note: You can't initiate sex whenever you want, but there are multiple times in GTA 6 when a sex scene is available to you, signified by double hearts over your home icon on the map or with certain limited-time onscreen prompts.

What leads to a sex scene? In my playthrough, twice these scenes happened while I was showering as one of the characters and the other asked if they could join me (and you can decide to let them or not). Another was after I reached a major milestone by contributing money to our savings account (hey, financial security is a major turn-on in real life, too!) and there was also a sex scene after a sizable heist. All of these happened while I was at a 4/4 "Hot Together" relationship status.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

You can also lose hearts from your relationship. This didn't happen often in my playthrough, but here's the ones I experienced:

According to Rockstar, if you want a strong relationship in GTA 6, you have to play both sides of that relationship. That means not just playing as Jason and doing nice things for Lucia, but also playing as Lucia and treating Jason well.

For my playthrough, where I reached the end of the game with a 4/4 "Hot Together" status, my stats show that I played nearly the exact same amount of time as Jason as I did Lucia.

Don't worry, this couple isn't joined at the hip. Both Lucia and Jason have missions, storylines, and activities they can (and are sometimes required to) complete alone. You can play plenty of GTA 6 as just a single character running around without the other, just remember to occasionally spend some time with your partner, respond to their texts, and switch to the other character from time to time.

But trust me, you'll want to spend lots of time together. Their relationship is fun to take part in, from both sides. Plus, doing crimes as a couple really pays off. It's helpful to have an extra set of hands to point guns at people, do crowd control during robberies, shoot out a cop's tires while driving, and carry off more loot than you could handle if you were rolling solo.

I'll be honest: I don't know how the game is different if you have a 4/4 relationship or a 1/4 relationship, because I've only played through the story once at this point, and I kept my relationship as strong as possible for nearly the entire game. We'll know more about the effects of a weak relationship as other players experiment with their relationship status, and we'll update this guide with what we find out.

#3642. Zara Tindall Shows Cheltenham Why She's The Queen of Race Day Dressing

Zara Tindall didn’t let the cold snap stop her from enjoying a day at the races on Friday. Accompanied by her close friend Dolly Maude and country-set favorite fashion designer Jade Holland Cooper, the daughter of Princess Anne and granddaughter of Queen Elizabeth II brought a dash of regal glamour to the proceedings following a glitzy night out in support of Prince William.

And while the sun may have been out, the Olympic equestrian still needed to wrap up against the chill. Tindall opted for a long plaid coat from L'Agence, a Purdey roll-neck jumper in brown, and a fascinator from Sally-Ann Provan. She accessorized with a new pair of Hector Lion earrings, a new Fairfax & Favor handbag, and completed the look with leather boots, also from Fairfax & Favor.

Zara Tindall joined in the action at Cheltenham Racecourse on Friday

Dolly, on the other hand, wore an avant-garde feather coat with knee-high boots and what looked to be a pair of emerald tights.

The pair were last spotted together in October, when they attended the William Hill Showcase Meeting at Cheltenham, but their friendship goes way back. Long considered Zara’s best friend, Dolly became Princess Anne’s lady-in-waiting in 2024. A former NHS midwife, she helped to deliver Zara’s third child, Lucas Tindall, on the floor of Zara’s bathroom at Gatcombe Park after the plan for the birth went awry in 2021.

Jade Holland Cooper and Zara Tindall on day one of The November Meeting at Cheltenham racecourse

But Dolly’s bond with the niece of King Charles III goes back long before that. (Not for nothing did Zara’s husband, Mike Tindall, joke that the 53-year-old is “more important than I am.”) Dolly was Zara’s maid of honor when the pair tied the knot, and when Zara split from her then-fiancé, jockey Richard Johnson, in 2003, the pair moved in together—they still live close by in the Cotswolds.

Having worked as a maternity practitioner in the NHS in Gloucestershire for 13 years, Dolly also did some philanthropic work using her maternity expertise, working in the unit of a hospital in Kambia, Sierra Leone for a month in 2013. At Kambia, she taught staff basic nursing skills. Before qualifying as a nurse, Dolly studied fashion and Cordon Bleu cookery at Eastbourne College of Food and Fashion, graduating in 1989.

Zara Tindall also braved the stormy weather for a day at Cheltenham with Dolly in October

Dolly Maude is known for her love of horses—a passion she shares with Zara and Princess Anne—and is often seen in Ascot’s royal box alongside the Princess Royal. In March 2024, she made her first official appearance as the Princess Royal’s lady-in-waiting, a momentous occasion that marked a new phase of her enduring bond with the royal family.

The royal confidant has four children with her husband Chris: Billy, who studied at Swansea University; Nell, who trained at the Central School of Ballet; a keen skier, Ted; and Mary.

Princess Anne's daughter wrapped up in a warm plaid coat and roll-neck jumper

Concerning Dolly’s appointment, another friend of Mrs. Maude's told The Telegraph, “She’s such a great girl. For the Princess Royal, it’s a perfect fit because of their shared love of dogs and horses. She’s not only extremely close to Zara, she also gets on brilliantly with the Princess. She’s fiercely loyal and discreet. It’s a great match.”

While much of Zara Tindall’s time this season has been spent touring the country’s most prestigious racing meets, she still found time to support her cousin, Prince William, at one of his treasured annual traditions. The Prince of Wales helped to put together the Tusk Conservation Awards at Raffles on Wednesday night and invited Zara to the celebration of conservation, alongside Lady Amelia and Lady Eliza Spencer and the Marchioness of Bath.

Dolly Maud made her debut as lady-in-waiting for the Princess Royal at the 2024 Commonwealth Day Service in March

Zara showcased her characteristically elegant style, donning a sapphire-blue Rebecca Vallance short-sleeved midi number, aptly named the “Crown Jewel” dress, which she paired with Kiki McDonough earrings. It is not the first time that the royal has lent her support to Prince William’s second-longest patronage: she also joined the crowd at the Tusk Awards in 2025, donning Rebecca Vallance again, and tearing up at the Prince of Wales’ speech in honor of those who gave their lives as rangers.

Zara Tindall and the Marchioness of Bath at the Tusk Awards

#3641. Former GTA 4 and Red Dead boss thinks "we are one Toy Story moment away" from people accepting gen-AI in game development in the West

"In the East, they've already accepted it."

Ben Feder, the former Take-Two CEO who oversaw the launch of massive hits like Grand Theft Auto 4, Red Dead Redemption, Borderlands, and BioShock during his tenure, believes the resistance against gen-AI in games will vanish once the games industry has its 'Toy Story moment'.

"When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business. "People didn't think it looked good. Then Pixar launched Toy Story. They created a movie that not only was awesome, but used computer-generated animation and chose a subject matter that made the most of it, and did an amazing job with it."

Feder argued that the success of Toy Story ended the resistance against computer-generated animation, and the same could happen to games. Feder added, "My own view is that we are one Toy Story moment away from consumer acceptance of AI in video games in the West. In the East, they've already accepted it."

Feder, who currently heads up venture capital fund Tirta Ventures, is investing in AI-first games. He, however, doesn't necessarily believe AI will reduce development costs, but that it also offers other advantages that could help game makers keep up with shifting consumer tastes.

"A lot of incumbents think about AI as a way of reducing costs, which it is," Feder said. "I query whether it will actually reduce costs, or will it just make games bigger for the same cost? But we're more interested in what AI can do to radically change gameplay."

Feder views gen-AI simply as new technology that allows developers to do things they couldn't before. He likened it to Unreal Engine's instancing technology, which allowed Fortnite and other battle royale games to support 100+ players in a single server.

"That's question number one as we think about what we invest in: Was this possible before AI?" Feder said of his VC firm's strategy. "And when AI gets better, does the game get better? That's harder for an incumbent to focus on, because they deploy a lot of capital, have enormous advantages in terms of distribution, capital, and IP, and all of that needs to be protected."

There's been enormous pushback from players, developers and pundits against the use of gen-AI in games. Even so, more and more studios have revealed using some gen-AI during development, such as to assist with coding. More broadly, gen-AI adoption is on the rise across the industry, with a recent report estimating 40 percent of developers are using it.

Some development studios, such as Fortnite maker Epic Games, have doubled down on the use of gen-AI in game development. Epic is even more bullish on gen-AI in its Unreal Engine, which the company is currently transforming into an engine that's almost entirely driven by gen-AI and LLMs. Consumer sentiment remains sour, however, and the perception of the tool is not helped by the number of 'AI slop' games taking over Steam's storefront, the 'enshittification' of fan wikis, or the link AI seems to have to the unprecedented wave of layoffs that has shaken the industry over the past two years.

#3640. It Took Me Over Three Hours To Walk Across GTA 6′s Massive Map

In some parts of the world, Grand Theft Auto 6 is out now on Xbox and PlayStation. And one of the biggest questions many players have is: How big is GTA 6‘s map? Well, I’ve walked, driven, and flown across the whole map to figure out just how long these journeys will take in Rockstar’s massive open-world sequel.

I doubt I need to explain what GTA 6 is or why so many people are excited to finally play it. So instead, let’s hop right into the numbers! First up, I walked across the whole map. To do this, I picked the most southern spot I could reach that was still on land and then made my way on foot as straight as possible without deviating. Sometimes, due to alligators or impossible-to-scale cliffs, I had to make small detours. And at first, I had to stick to highways as I worked my way up the islands that make up the bottom part of GTA 6‘s massive world. But once I got past that, I was able to mostly head north on foot without much issue. When I reached the furthest point north on the map, I stopped my timer.

It took me 3 hours, 21 minutes, and 20 seconds to walk across GTA 6. It was quite the journey, and during my walk I discovered areas I had never seen before and encountered new events, including a dude having sex with an anime character while wearing a VR headset.

After walking, I turned around and then ran across the map. I followed a similar route and also had to dodge alligators and other critters. Even running and sprinting constantly, it still took me 1 hour and 41 minutes. In comparison, running across GTA V‘s map takes about 30 minutes. And walking across it takes around two and a half hours. You might be wondering why I was able to run across GTA V‘s world in less than one-third the time I was able to run across GTA 6‘s, while walking didn’t result in quite so dramatic a discrepancy. I think it comes down to the fact that characters in GTA V can sprint forever and seem to move faster. In GTA 6, Jason and Lucia have a stamina bar that limits how far they can sprint at full speed and seem to move a bit slower.

Next up, I grabbed a mid-range sedan, hopped in as Lucia and, starting from the southernmost roadway on the map, I drove the highways and freeways all the way up to the most northern dirt road in the game. To drive across the map via the highway, it took 10 minutes and 53 seconds.

To be clear: I wasn’t following speed limits and I weaved around traffic like a lunatic. Still, it took nearly 11 minutes of highway driving at top speed to cross the whole map. In comparison, you can find videos of people driving quickly across GTA V‘s map in about eight minutes.

Finally, I grabbed a prop plane and flew from the furthest bit of land in the south to the furthest bit of land in the north of Leonida. This journey took 5 minutes and 51 seconds.

I imagine some people are going to use these numbers to try to compare this world to those of past GTA games. And some might be disappointed that GTA 6‘s map doesn’t take an hour to drive across. But trust me, as someone who has played over 130 hours of GTA 6, the map feels massive. I booted up GTA V recently to compare, and that game feels so tiny and empty in comparison.

These times also don’t do a good job of demonstrating how big GTA 6 is in every direction. There are more buildings to enter, underwater locations to explore, and large swaths of wilderness to explore. So while these numbers are interesting, they don’t tell the whole story.

If you were worried GTA 6 is small, just know that after playing 100 hours and finishing the story and most of the main side missions, I still have sections on my map I’ve yet to visit.

Johnny Depp is officially back in Hollywood, at least as far as his career is concerned. His 2026 movie release, Ebenezer, just topped the domestic box office, marking his first major studio release in eight years. But while the actor is making his way back onto movie screens (even for lesser pay), he's apparently in no hurry to return to living in the United States. In fact, he's been spending most of his time somewhere that sounds an awful lot like a vacation destination.

The Pirates of the Caribbean star recently spoke with The Wall Street Journal about his childhood, his unlikely introduction to acting and where he calls home these days. I knew Depp owned an island in the Bahamas, but I hadn't realized just how much time he actually spends there. According to the 63-year-old actor:

Today, I live most of the time in the Bahamas. It’s where I’ve found total peace and quiet. Nobody's pointing a camera at me or staring.

I suppose having your own island makes avoiding the paparazzi considerably easier. And considering how much attention Depp's personal life has received over the years, I can understand why he'd want somewhere he can go about his day without somebody pointing a camera at him.

Yet what I found particularly interesting was how the Oscar nominee described the property itself. Depp purchased Little Hall's Pond Cay, a 45-acre island in the Bahamas, in 2004 for a reported $3.6 million. And while I pictured some enormous Caribbean mansion, his description of the place sounds surprisingly modest. He continued:

I bought my 1940s wood house in 2004 and added a yurt and a painting studio. Art continues to be a sanctuary that lets me process the world around me.

A wooden house, a yurt and somewhere to paint. Not exactly what I would have pictured for the man who spent years playing one of Disney's most recognizable characters, but I can appreciate the appeal.

Depp also told the publication that he enjoys reading and playing guitar in his music studio, which sounds about right for somebody who originally moved to Los Angeles hoping to make it as a musician.

Forget Scrooge, Johnny Depp Will Soon Be Back On The Big Screen For What May Be His Scariest Role Ever

His current living situation is especially interesting considering how frequently his family moved when he was growing up. Depp recalled relocating approximately 40 times during his childhood, particularly after his family moved from Kentucky to Florida. The constant changes made it difficult to settle in, and he described himself as an outsider.

Music eventually became his escape. His mother gave him an acoustic guitar when he was 12, and by 1983, Depp had moved to Los Angeles with his band, hoping to make a career out of playing music. Then he met Nicolas Cage.

According to Depp, the two became friends after Cage started attending his band's performances. Eventually, Cage suggested that he try acting and helped connect him with an agent. That led to his film debut in 1984's A Nightmare on Elm Street, followed by the career that made him one of Hollywood's biggest stars.

Of course, his relationship with Hollywood became considerably more complicated in recent years. Depp stepped away from major American studio productions amid legal battles with his ex-wife, Amber Heard, including their highly publicized 2022 defamation trial. He continued working internationally, appearing in the French film Jeanne du Barry and directing Modi: Three Days on the Wing of Madness.

Now, he's back with Ti West's Ebenezer, which opened Nov. 13 and earned an estimated $19 million domestically during its first weekend. But does the box-office win signal a larger Hollywood comeback? Only time will tell, but Depp has another major American release on the horizon: Day Drinker, a thriller co-starring Penélope Cruz, arriving on the 2027 movie schedule. Still, his latest comments suggest returning to American movies doesn't necessarily mean returning to a US address.

The '80s heartthrob has owned his Bahamian retreat for more than two decades, so this isn't some sudden relocation following his Hollywood troubles. But hearing him describe how much time he spends there gives a better idea of what his life looks like these days. After years of playing Jack Sparrow, I suppose it's fitting that Johnny Depp found a little peace on an island of his own.

Ebenezer is now playing in theaters, so check your local listings for showtimes. If you want to revisit Depp's iconic portrayal of Captain Jack, all the Pirates of the Caribbean films stream with a Disney+ subscription.

#3638. Blizzard suspends World of Warcraft: Forever gold exploit abusers, puts trading blocks on their accounts and removes ill-gotten funds for good measure

Players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard. Suspensions have been issued, trade locks have been put on accounts, and ill-gotten gold is being seized.

For those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the new late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold. By quickly clearing select mobs with area-of-effect damage, players would loot upwards of 100 raw gold an hour. This exploit, clearly not intentional, was nonetheless farmed until Blizzard hotfixed it earlier in the week.

There was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit. That speculation would come to an end late last night with an official statement from the World of Warcraft: Forever development team.

"As players continue their journey into WoW Forever’s higher-level content, we are closely monitoring the game economy to ensure that gold sources and costs are well balanced," the statement reads. "Finding efficient farming spots has always been part of the game, and is how most players have earned their epic mounts since 2004. When a single location proves so lucrative that it overshadows all other sources, we generally adjust it to bring it in line with the rest."

It goes on to explain the nature of the bug that made this gold farm possible, before reassuring those who may have accidentally benefited from some extra cash from their regular runs of Blackmaw Hold they have nothing to worry about. The same cannot be said for those who took advantage of the situation.

"Players who simply ran Blackmaw Hold a few times and benefited organically from the extra loot did nothing wrong, and no one should worry that they’re putting their account at risk if they accidentally benefit from a bug," it continues. "But there were a couple hundred players worldwide who recognized that this was unintended and spent significant time exclusively farming that group of enemies.

"Yesterday, we put an economy lock on their accounts to prevent broader impact to the game economy while we investigated the extent of the exploitative gains, including gold earned by vendoring bugged drops. Today, we are in the process of removing all such gold earned, as well as applying account suspensions to significant abusers."

The post concludes by thanking players for their feedback on the matter, and a final warning: "As always, we advise all players to refrain from abusing game mechanics that are clearly unintended. We will continue to take action against intentional abuse."

This decision certainly sets the precedent moving forward with World of Warcraft: Forever that such exploits won't be tolerated, and rolling back the wealth of those who made out of Blackmaw Hold like bandits is a good measure that should prevent continuous damage.

Inevitably the exploit would have had some impact, specifically in those days prior to trading blocks being put in place. While the gold on the exploiter's accounts may be removed, any purchases they made on the in-game auction house will have affected others through buying and selling goods with ample funds.

Those who were suspended temporarily will be able to regain access to the game by the time the first wave of raids come out in December, so it very much feels like a firm slap on the wrist in that regard. Even so, given the establishment of punishments for such behavior, one can only wonder if future events will come with harsher penalties.

World of Warcraft: Forever, despite this small economic roadbump, is proving exceptionally popular for Blizzard. It's already broken records for the series, and has impressed players so far with its revamping of the classic MMO.

#3637. We Tested How Long It Takes To Run Out Of Gas In GTA 6

Grand Theft Auto 6 is a massive game! It takes about an hour and a half to sprint across the map. But most players will be driving around Vice City, and this time around, GTA 6 demands that you monitor your gas tank while cruising the streets and highways of Leonida. So how long before you need to fill up in GTA 6, and does it get annoying?

To test this out, I booted up Grand Theft Auto 6 and hopped into two different cars. First, I tested a basic and somewhat older pickup truck. I found a loop of highway near the southern part of Vice City and filled up my gas tank at a local station. Then, the journey began. For this test, I drove around like I normally do in GTA 6 when not being shot at or racing someone. I also tried really hard not to stop, but traffic is traffic, and sometimes I had to slow down or completely brake. I wanted to avoid damaging the engines of any vehicles during testing so as not to toss in yet another variable.

It took 29 minutes and 8 seconds for the pickup to run out of gas completely.

To provide some context: You can drive across the entire map of GTA 6 via its highways and with a lead foot in under 15 minutes. So, in theory, I think I could drive across the map twice before running out of gas.

For my next test, I swapped out the older pickup truck for a Banshee, a fast-as-heck sports car that has been a part of the franchise since at least GTA 3. I loaded up the gas tank and hit the same highway loop as before. I went faster in the Banshee, of course, but still avoided crashing and stopping as much as possible. I may have had to restart the test at one point when I slammed into a minivan and basically blew up my engine. Science is dangerous.

In GTA 6, while driving a Banshee sports car, it took 18 minutes and 31 seconds to drain my tank entirely.

So, assuming I don’t hit a minivan again, that’s enough time to drive across the entire map via highways and still have some fuel left over to get to a nearby station and fill up.

Finally, I grabbed an electric car modeled after a Tesla 3, found a nearby charging station, got the battery juiced up, and hit that same highway loop one more time. Luckily, I didn’t crash at all during this test, and after following the same rules as before, it took 20 minutes and 23 seconds.

Personally, across over 130 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6, I only ran out of gas once, not counting these tests. I ran out of battery once as well. In both cases they were stolen cars that didn’t have full tanks and I was too busy dodging cops to notice I was running out of go-go juice or zoom liquid. I also had a few moments where I got low on gas during getaways and had to change plans or vehicles to accommodate.

But for the most part, I forgot vehicles needed fuel when playing GTA 6. And the game does a good job of letting you know when you hit halfway and when you’re nearing empty, even marking the nearest station on the compass to help you get fueled up ASAP. There are also a lot of gas stations around, so I was rarely too far away to reach one. Also, if I was driving a personal vehicle that I owned, I could just use the in-game Scooter Bros app to request another one of my vehicles. And when, a bit later, I summoned back the car in which I’d run low on gas via that same app, it would have some extra fuel in the tank. Nifty.

So I never found the fuel tank (or battery management) annoying at all. In the early hours, when money is tight and car options are limited, it proved a bit more of a hassle. But later on, it stopped being a problem. If anything, it added a fun variable that could derail a robbery if I wasn’t being careful or cause me to ditch a stolen car for another option. I doubt it will cause most players too much annoyance.

These include the Dinka Endura military motorcycle and the Crest Kayak.

This is an upgrade from Jason's Vapid Ganado vehicle with exclusive mods and classic stylings.

This Lake Leonida mod shop specialises in off-road modifications and hand painted customisation.

Another mod shop, specialising in detailed interiors, exquisite rims, and "donk stylings".

A clothing store in Stockyard that includes various unique looks for Jason and Lucia.

#3635. "We'd love to have you" - New Zealand's tourist board gives a nod to those hopping timezones to play Grand Theft Auto 6 early

New Zealand's tourism board has taken advantage of all the excitement surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6's launch, as hordes of players who've changed their Xbox timezones to that of the world's second best rugby team (sorry) to jump into the game early.

"One perk of seeing the sun first? Getting GTA 6 first too," reads a post on the New Zealand tourist board's Instagram account: PureNewZealand. "We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us. We get it, and we'd love to have you." The post also includes a video of folks looking at all the natural beauty of New Zealand, presumably before they all look themselves indoors to play the video game, alongside the caption: "life, because we're getting GTA 6 first."

For those unaware, Xbox owners have been swapping their console time zones for years to New Zealand in order to take advantage of the region's access to games before anywhere else in the world. When games have, let's say, a worldwide release time of midnight across all nations, those living in New Zealand are able to jump in first as a result.

Microsoft has for years been happy to let this practice continue on its platform, and as such a sort of cultural norm about hopping on a digital plane for a game's release has been established. If you want guidance, we have a guide on how to pull off the GTA 6 New Zealand trick yourself which can walk you through it.

If you aren't keen on doing so for whatever reason, you can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 too. If you want one final run through on what to expect from Rockstar's big release last minute, our Everything We Know about Grand Theft Auto 6 page should set you right for good measure.
