Ashley Hebert and J.P. Rosenbaum got engaged during the season 7 finale of The Bachelorette in 2011. The following year, the twosome tied the knot in December 2012 and their nuptials were documented for a TV special. Ashley gave birth to their first child, a baby boy named Fordham, in September 2014. The pair welcomed their second child, a daughter named Essex, in November 2016. In August 2018, Ashley and J.P. renewed their vows during a trip to Aruba.

Ashley revealed that JP was diagnosed with Guillain-Barré syndrome, a rare neurological disorder, is a condition in which the body’s immune system attacks the nerves, in December 2019. “He is in treatment and doing well,” the pediatric dentist said at the time. “It may be a long road to full recovery, but we are so grateful to everyone that has helped us get to a speedy diagnosis and treatment.”

JP, for his part, detailed his symptoms during a December hospital stay: “Things you do every day, like picking up this phone, or buttoning buttons, tying shoelaces, putting on deodorant, just can’t do it. Picking up my kids, can’t do it.” He was discharged on December 9, 2019.

In March 2022, the dentist revealed that she has had a boyfriend for nearly one year.

Credit: Courtesy of Emily Maynard/Instagram

After ending her brief engagement to Brad Womack, Emily Maynard was named the eighth Bachelorette in 2012. She accepted a proposal from Jef Holm during the finale, but the twosome ended their relationship several months after the season finished airing. In June 2014, Emily, who has a daughter named Ricki from her previous relationship, married Tyler Johnson. The couple have since welcomed three sons: Jennings, Gibson and Gatlin. Emily gave birth to the couple’s first daughter, her fifth child, in October 2020.

In October 2016, the duo, who reside in Seattle, welcomed their son Asher. Desiree, who works as a wedding dress designer, announced in 2018 that she was pregnant with the pair’s second son. Us broke the news in January 2019 that Desiree gave birth to a second son named Zander. She announced in May 2024 that she was expecting baby No. 3. Son Noah was born in November 2024.

Desiree Hartsock accepted a proposal from Chris Siegfried during season 9 of The Bachelorette in 2013. Less than two years later, they wed in January 2015. In October 2016, the duo, who reside in Seattle, welcomed their son Asher. Desiree, who works as a wedding dress designer, announced in 2018 that she was pregnant with the pair’s second son.

Us broke the news in January 2019 that Desiree gave birth to a second son named Zander. She announced in May 2024 that she was expecting baby No. 3. Son Noah was born in November 2024.

The Georgia-based attorney Andi Dorfman was named the 10th Bachelorette in 2014. Andi accepted a proposal from Josh Murray during the finale. While the pair moved in together in Atlanta, they announced their split in January 2015. Andi documented her Bachelor/Bachelorette journey in her first book, It’s Not Okay, released in 2016. She released her second book, Single State of Mind, in 2018.  “Life after The Bachelorette has been a wild ride for me. People often ask if the show was good or bad for my life and without hesitation, I always say good,” Andi told Us exclusively. “I know had it not been for The Bachelorette I wouldn’t be living life in New York City and being able to say that I am an author working on my third book. And as each season goes on, I may feel a little older but feel proud and grateful to have been part of a show that has so many devoted fans and is still beloved by so many people.”  Andi added that she still speaks to “a lot of people from [her] season,” former host Harrison and a lot of fellow Bachelorettes. “Between the 13 of us, we’ve built a nice, supportive community that I didn’t expect but definitely cherish,” she explained. “Fan encounters are interesting because living in New York the vibe is less fanatic and people are too busy or in too much of a hurry to stop you, but my parents, who live in Georgia, still get people that will recognize their last name or recognize them from being on television, so I think in a funny way they are more of the stars than I am.”  In June 2020, Andi announced via Instagram that she made to move from NYC to Los Angeles. After reconnecting with an old friend named Blaine Hart in Italy during summer 2021, the pair started dating. He proposed on the beach in L.A. in March 2022. The following May, the duo tied the knot in Italy, the same place where they reconnected two years prior.  On August 4, 2024, Andi shared via Instagram that she and Hart were expecting their first child, who arrived in December of that year.

During the season 11 premiere of The Bachelorette, the men met both Kaitlyn Bristowe and fellow season 19 Bachelor contestant Britt Nilsson. The contestants then voted for Kaitlyn to be the lead for the season. During the finale, both Shawn Booth and Nick Viall got down on one knee, but Kaitlyn accepted a ring from Shawn. The pair moved to Nashville and started their lives together offscreen. Fan speculation that the couple called it quits surfaced in summer 2018, but Kaitlyn, who hosts a podcast titled “Off the Vine,” and Shawn, who opened up a gym in Nashville, did not announce the end of their engagement until November 2018. Due to the fact that the pair were together more than two years, Kaitlyn was the first woman from the franchise who got to keep her Neil Lane engagement ring after the breakup even though she did not marry Shawn.  The former Bachelorette confirmed her relationship with fellow Bachelor Nation star Jason Tartick in January 2019. Months later, the duo — who exchanged “I love yous” in April 2019 — moved in together in Nashville and announced they adopted a dog. They adopted a second pup in December 2019. In June 2020, Kaitlyn confirmed that she and Jason picked out an engagement ring before she left to film season 29 of Dancing With the Stars. Almost a year later, the former banker finally popped the question during a May 2021 "Off the Vine" recording session. “It was everything I could have asked for,” Bristowe told Entertainment Tonight. “The words that came out of his mouth were insanely beautiful. We’ve never locked eyes like that in our lives. We were holding hands, so intense, and I was listening to his every word, but still blacked out.” The duo announced their split in August 2023. "Continuing our friendship is incredibly important to both of us," they wrote in a joint social media post at the time. "We feel grateful to be ending our engagement with love and respect for each other. It’s heartbreaking and sad to say goodbye, but our care and admiration for one another will never die."

JoJo Fletcher accepted a proposal from Jordan Rodgers during the season 12 finale of The Bachelorette in 2012. The twosome moved to Dallas together, but as of January 2019, have no concrete wedding plans. In November 2018, JoJo, who recently launched a clothing line, told Us exclusively that she and Jordan would consider having a televised wedding.  “I would never say no, never, but I think it’s very important that, if it was a televised wedding, that it stays true and organic to us,” she explained. “We would never do a wedding that was just filled with a bunch of Bachelor people that we don’t even know, because that’s not us. But, if we could have it the exact way that we’d want it to be, and allow people to see it as well, then I would say yes.” After Jordan re-proposed in August 2019, the Cash Pad stars told Us that they plan to wed in June 2020. Their nuptials were postponed, however, amid the coronavirus pandemic. Fletcher and Rodgers finally wed in May 2022. Three years later, the couple announced they were expecting their first baby. Daughter Romy Blair arrived in December 2025.

Rachel Lindsay and Bryan Abasolo got engaged during the season 13 finale of The Bachelorette in 2017. “It’s, like, we’re either going to have this 500-plus wedding that we want, or it’s going to be super small,” Rachel said of the duo's nuptials in December 2018. “So I’m going to hurt a lot of feelings, but I’m going to have the wedding that we want, surrounded by the people we love the most and I want to do it as soon as possible. I don’t want to put off a wedding because I’m planning something big for everybody else.” The twosome ultimately tied the knot in August 2019 in Mexico. Rachel, who splits her time between Miami and Los Angeles, works for Extra and hosts the “Higher Learning” podcast with Van Lathan. In January 2022, she released a book titled Miss Me With That: Hot Takes, Helpful Tidbits, and a Few Hard Truths.  Bryan filed for divorce from Rachel in January 2024 after four years of marriage and requested spousal support. Rachel said at the time that she would “eventually” share further details of the split but for the moment was “trying to take it day by day.”

Becca Kufrin accepted a proposal from Garret Yrigoyen during the season 14 finale of The Bachelorette in 2018. The couple told Us exclusively in December 2018 that they have no plans to tie the knot yet. “No dates, no months, no venue,” she said at the time. “The only thing that we’ve talked about that we want are food trucks. I want a great taco truck and a ton of Skee-Ball machines so everyone can just play games.” In August 2019, the pair moved to San Diego together and adopted a Corgi puppy named Miss Minno.  The twosome made headlines in June 2020 after Becca and Rachel recorded an emotional podcast about the Black Lives Matter movement, in which they discussed Garrett’s public support for police. “For those who are curious about my relationship with Garrett at this point, all I can say right now is I don’t know,” Becca said in June 2020." I can’t give anything more than that. It’s something that we are trying to work through and discuss and do work on at home at this time and that’s where the work will remain and that’s really the best can give you at this point.” Three months later, Becca confirmed that the pair went their separate ways. “After many conversations, we came to this decision. It wasn’t something that we just arrived at one night,” Becca explained on the “Bachelor Happy Hour” podcast. “It wasn’t based solely off of one Instagram post or somebody else’s opinions or comments. There’s much more to it. To any relationship, there’s a lot of layers, and it’s not for me to divulge details. It’s no one’s business other than what I’m telling you right now.” Becca returned to ABC for season 7 of Bachelor in Paradise and met boyfriend Thomas Jacobs. Becca proposed to Jacobs in May 2022 after less than a year of dating. Five months later, Thomas popped the question to Becca during a beach trip to Ojai, California.  The duo announced in April 2023 that they were expecting their first child. Their baby boy was born in September 2023. One month later, the twosome said “I do” at a San Diego courthouse. Kufrin revealed in October 2025 that she and Jacobs were expecting their second baby. Their second son, Steven, was born in April 2026.

Former pageant queen Hannah Brown, who was the 15th Bachelorette, broke off her engagement to winner Jed Wyatt during the July 2019 finale after learning he had a girlfriend at home. Hannah and partner Alan Bersten took home the mirrorball trophy during the November 2019 finale. Hannah went public with model boyfriend Adam Woolard in February 2021. She published a memoir titled God Bless This Mess: Learning to Live and Love Through Life's Best (and Worst) Moments in November 2021. Hairstylist Clare Crawley's unprecedented season 16 journey came to an early end after she fell in love with Dale Moss when there was still 16 men remaining. During a November 2020 episode, Harrison gave Clare and Dale one-on-one time and she ultimately broke things off with the other suitors and accepted a proposal from Dale (and Tayshia Adams took over where Clare left off.) In November 2020, the pair announced via Instagram Live that they recently celebrated three months together and were house hunting in Sacramento, California. Their happiness was short-lived, however. Clare and Dale ended their engagement in January 2021. “We appreciate the love and support we’ve received from so many people, but this is the healthiest decision for both of us at this time,” Dale wrote via Instagram at the time. A month later, Us exclusively revealed that the twosome are back together after they were spotted holding hands in Florida. Less than one year after giving things another shot, Us confirmed in September 2021 that Clare and Dale split again. One year later, Us revealed Clare was dating a man named Ryan Dawkins. He proposed in Las Vegas in October 2022. Clare and Ryan wed in February 2023. Clare announced via Instagram in July 2023 that she and Ryan are expecting their first baby via surrogate. “Our laundry is about to get a whole lot cuter in 2024!!” she captioned a video of the couple putting a onesie on a clothesline that read, “Worth the wait.” Clare confirmed her daughter’s arrival in January 2024. “She’s here!” she wrote via Instagram, sharing a photo that showed her hugging Ryan in a hospital room.

#3592. All Eyes Were On The OG Hunger Games Cast At Premiere, But I Need To Talk About THAT Floating Shoulder

We’ve known for a while that Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson would be returning for a small gig in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping. But knowing something will happen and seeing it on the carpet are two separate things. Of course, all eyes were on the two original stars (and Elizabeth Banks and Woody Harrelson) during last night’s New York premiere. To the point I almost missed the coolest floating shoulder dress.

Note I said shoulder and not shoulders. We’ve seen Florence Pugh and Emily Blunt rock the plural version before, but Sunrise on the Reaping’s Whitney Peak took the look to a new level and used the fashion trend as a perch for a white bird on the movie's (fittingly) purple carpet. Take a look.

The perched bird really fits into the vibe the ladies of Panem have created in recent weeks. Mckenna Grace has dropped all the Hunger Games looks, and paid homage to Jennifer Lawrence many times. Elle Fanning has gotten into the Capitol-themed dressing in recent weeks. The whole thing has been really fun to watch play out. Now, Whitney Peak, who plays Haymitch’s “love” Lenore Dove – herself a mirror to Lucy Gray – has her own viral look.

Of course, even when you are wearing a gorgeous deep blue gown with perfect theming and an intricate shoulder, it’s hard to compete with the fan service of seeing the OGs on a Hunger Games carpet again. It’s difficult to believe it’s been 11 years since the last Katniss Everdeen story graced the big screen, but time has passed. The cast still looks great, though.

Suzanne Collins’ return to Panem with Sunrise on the Reaping was an exceptionally well-reviewed (if a bit bleak) book. The trailer for Reaping has looked astounding and first reactions are coming in. The movie officially hits the 2026 release schedule on November 20th, and while this was the big premiere, I hope that means we have a couple more days of fun celebrity fashion to go.

She loves a good animated movie. Jessica has a Masters in Library Science degree from Indiana University, and used to be found behind a reference desk most definitely not shushing people. She now uses those skills in researching and tracking down information in very different ways.

#3591. Robert Pattinson Is the New James Bond

It looks like Robert Pattinson is trading in his Batmobile for an Aston Martin. After a highly scrutinized and lengthy audition process involving some of Hollywood’s most sought-after leading men, it was the Batman star who emerged at the eleventh hour to nab the role of MI6 agent James Bond.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” said Pattinson in a statement. “I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

Created by Ian Fleming for his 1953 novel Casino Royale, James Bond, the British intelligence officer who lends his immense talents to MI6, is one of the most recognizable characters in the modern world. Figuring prominently in 12 of Fleming’s novels and two collections of short stories, Bond is both tall, dark, and handsome and calm, cool, and collected—the platonic ideal of a world-class spy. Bond leapt from page to screen in 1962 with the Eon-produced Dr. No, spawning one of the biggest media franchises in history. Since its inception, the 27 Bond films have grossed more than $7 billion dollars worldwide.

Pattinson follows in the suave footsteps of Daniel Craig, who played James Bond for five films, from 2006’s Casino Royale until 2021’s No Time to Die where (spoiler alert) Craig’s 007 dies while protecting the world from a global terrorist organization. Around No Time to Die, there was another shake up in Bond ownership when Amazon acquired Bond’s parent studio, MGM, in an $8.5 billion deal. Barbara Broccoli—whose father, Eon founder Albert R. “Cubby” Broccoli, produced the first Bond film—and her half brother, Michael G. Wilson, held the rights to the franchise for almost 30 years, and pledged to work with Amazon. However, in February 2025, Broccoli and Wilson announced that they’d be stepping back from the franchise and ceding complete creative control to Amazon MGM. At the Oscars a month later, the Broccoli family was honored with a bizarre musical tribute to James Bond, starring Margaret Qualley, Doja Cat, and Lisa, unofficially ushering in a new era in the Bond Cinematic Universe.

Although a new era of Bond loomed, Amazon MGM had one major problem: They needed a new Bond. Ahead of No Time to Die, Craig had announced that he was stepping away from the franchise, leaving the producers with a 007-sized hole to fill. Before she stepped away, Broccoli insinuated that this new era of Bond was looking for a younger actor, in their 30s, to take over the reins from Craig, who was 51 when he retired from MI6.

Technically, they landed on someone slightly outside their preferred age range; Pattinson is 40 years old. Just don’t tell him that. During Vanity Fair’s lie detector test with Jennifer Lawrence while promoting their film Die My Love, Pattinson insisted he was from a different generation. I am Gen Z,” he said to Lawrence. “I am.” Hey, you’re only as old as you feel. In the same video, Pattinson said he “likes taking jobs of younger actors,” which he managed to do with his Bond casting. Good for Pattinson.

Almost every leading man in Hollywood’s name came up as a potential predecessor to Craig—except for Pattinson, who the masses assumed was out of contention due to the fact that he locked into playing another beloved fictional character with massive IP: Batman. Pattinson’s take on the caped crusader in Matt Reeve’s The Batman (2022) was a major success, but several production delays on The Batman Part II, and a shakeup at Batman’s studio, DC—last week, it was announced that the co-CEOs of DC Productions, James Gunn and Peter Safran, were ousted from the studio—meant that there might be time in Pattinson’s schedule for some sexy espionage.

Still, it was far from a done deal that Pattinson would land 007. In recent years, some fans have advocated for a twist on the classic Bond formula. Lashana Lynch made history as Nomi, the first Black person to ever to hold the 007 moniker, in No Time to Die. But Nomi is not James Bond. There was a seemingly endless period when the world was convinced that Idris Elba—arguably the most tall, dark, and handsome man to ever exist—would take on the mantle at some point, but it wasn’t meant to be. Now, at 53, Elba has seemingly aged out of the role. (For the record, Elba thought the next Bond should be a woman.) Elba wasn’t the only name bandied about in recent years. It was reported in 2024 that Aaron Taylor-Johnson was close to signing a contract to take over the role, but those reports were never confirmed.

Although a favorite at the beginning, Jacob Elordi reportedly didn’t screen test for the role. Riz Ahmed made an Emmy-nominated television show, Bait, inspired by the idea of a British Pakistani actor getting cast as Bond. Other actors rumored to be in the mix over the course of the process include, but are not limited to, Tom Francis, Harris Dickinson, and, apparently, Harry Styles. At the end of the day, five actors reportedly screen-tested for the role: Slow Horse’s Jack Lowden, One Night Only’s Callum Turner, Disclosure Day’s Josh O’Connor, Superman’s Nicholas Hoult, and Pattison. Hoult and Pattinson were the last names to emerge as contenders for the role, implying that the powers that be at Amazon MGM may not have been happy with the three options presented and sent a hail mary. When Puck reported that Pattinson was able to negotiate a three-picture deal rather than a four-picture deal despite commanding a much higher salary than the other options, it looked like the writing was on the wall that Pattinson would be the next Bond.

It also helps that Pattinson is having a career high at the moment, having starred in a handful of the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful films of 2026. He began the year by turning his controversial A24 comedy The Drama with Zendaya into a box-office success, generating $134 million worldwide on a reported budget of about $28 million. He then followed that up with a deliciously sniveling turn in Christopher Nolan’s epic The Odyssey, an Oscar front-runner that earned $1.8 billion at the box office. Then there’s Primetime, the Lance Oppenheim drama starring Pattinson as To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen. (Yes, in a way, Chris Hansen is now one degree from being James Bond. Let that sink in). Primetime hit big with $62 million globally on an $14.5 million budget, and is earning Pattinson leading-actor buzz. On top of it all, he’s still got Dune: Part Three with Denis Villeneuve coming down the pipeline in December.

Ultimately, the Twilight star was handpicked by the powers that be at Amazon MGM, including producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman and director Denis Villeneuve, who is helming the next iteration of the series based on a script from screenwriter Steven Knight, with Tanya Lapointe executive producing. Given the fact that Pattinson is starring in Villeneuve’s highly-anticipated Dune: Part Three, it might not be that much of a surprise that the director chose Pattinson as his next Bond. “Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey,” said Villeneuve in a statement. “We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.”

Pattinson enters a long lineage of spectacularly suave spies—some who lasted longer than others in Bond’s impeccably tailored suits. The first-ever James Bond was, of course, Sean Connery, who went on to star in six Bond films, including From Russia With Love (1963), Goldfinger (1964), and Diamonds Are Forever (1971). Connery was followed by George Lazenby, who starred in a single Bond film, On Her Majesty’s Secret Service (1969), before passing the reins back to Connery. The third Bond was Roger Moore, who took over for 1973’s Live and Let Die, and appeared in a total of seven Bond films, most notably The Spy Who Loved Me (1977) and Octopussy (1983).

After Moore came Timothy Dalton, who became 007 with 1987’s The Living Daylights, then threw in the towel after 1989’s License to Kill. Millennials will fondly remember the next Bond: Pierce Brosnan, who starred as the sexy spy in four films from 1995’s GoldenEye to 2002’s Die Another Day, until Craig took over in 2006.

Will Pattison’s Bond be more debonair like Brosnan, who told VF he was “eagerly” awaiting the Bond casting news, or brooding like Craig? Will he be remembered as a rightful heir to Connery’s throne, or will his Bond feel closer to Austin Powers in The Spy Who Shagged Me? In any case, let’s hope Pattinson prefers his martinis shaken not stirred. He’s going to be drinking a lot of them for the foreseeable future.

#3589. An NES Power Glove Just Became The Most Dangerous Weapon In Pro Wrestling

All Elite Wrestling's recent Full Gear event had no shortage of great moments, but Austin Creed stole the show with a move straight out of Street Fighter. After teaming up with his Next Level partner Kofi Kingston and Swerve Strickland to take on Bandido, Hangman Adam Page, and Brody King in a Texas Death Match, anything went in this brawl — including vintage NES accessories.

Looking the worse for wear at King's hands, Creed busted out an NES Power Glove and landed a Shoryuken uppercut that exploded in a shower of sparks, knocking his burly foe flat on his back. The moment quickly went viral, and Creed's team would eventually triumph, emerging as the AEW World Trios Champions.

Creed is no stranger to video games; during his run with WWE, he ran the Up Up Down Down YouTube channel, where he competed with fellow performers in a wide variety of games. Wrestling and video games have formed a symbiotic relationship over the years, with top performers like Kenny Omega referencing games like Street Fighter and Final Fantasy 7 for his signature moves. Video games have also positively influenced professional wrestlers, with top WWE star Roman Reigns saying it's a popular downtime activity with his fellow wrestlers and better than some of the "extracurricular" exploits of previous generations.

In another video game crossover, former WWE champion Cody Rhodes played Guile in the live-action Street Fighter movie, which was released last month, and he even cosplayed as the character at WWE SummerSlam. Sadly, the film wasn't a big box-office hit, making only $100.7 million worldwide during its run (via Box Office Mojo). In comparison, the other Capcom-based movie, Resident Evil, was far more successful, generating over $416 million worldwide and making it the highest-grossing Resident Evil movie of all time.

The comic spoke out after Musk shared his thoughts.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The newest Saturday Night Live episode aired last weekend, with comedian John Mulaney serving as Season 52’s latest host and Phoebe Bridgers performing as the musical guest. Unsurprisingly, the episode began with a cold open centered around recent events, and it centered on the controversy surrounding Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang. As part of that segment, Elon Musk was lampooned by the show again and, after he expressed disappointment with the impression, cast member Jeremy Culhane reacted.

SNL’s latest cold open sees the CIA gathering the U.S’ biggest tech magnates for a training session on not exposing secrets to potential operatives. The presiding official (played by Mulaney) speaks to Musk (Jeremy Culhane), Mark Zuckerberg (Andrew Dismukes), Sam Altman (Ben Marshall), Dario Amodei (Jane Wickline) and Peter Thiel (James Austin Johnson). After Mulaney’s character unsuccessfully tries to make his case, Huang (played by returning cast member Bowen Yang) warns his colleagues using his own experience.

Ultimately, the real Elon Musk appeared to be less than impressed with the sketch, in which Mulaney’s character used venn diagrams to explain to the CEOs that a woman wouldn’t truly be interested in them without an ulterior motive. In response, Musk dropped a comment under the sketch on X and included a diagram of his own:

@nbcsnl lol https://t.co/7vw3wS9Jm3November 16, 2026

Throughout the sketch, Culhane’s Musk makes several random statements at the fictional briefing, one of which sees him compare himself to James Bond and another in which he tries to connect with Huang over their leather jackets. It’s because of those random asides that both the CIA official and even Huang use spray bottles on Culhane’s Musk. On X, after someone ranked the performances the actual SpaceX founder shared his take on Culhane’s impression, writing:

I’d give them maybe 5/10 for me. They need to try harder.

This isn’t the first time Musk has taken issue with an impression of himself on Saturday Night Live. Back in late 2024, the tech mogul – who also hosted SNL in 2021 – called out Dana Carvey for his take on him. The following year would also see Musk chastise Mike Meyers’ impression of him as well. The Tesla figurehead is far from the only star to ever take issue with an impression, as Kanye West disliked Chris Redd’s impression of him Also, Ice Cube was dismissive of Kenan Thompson’s take on him.

After this latest Musk impression, Jeremy Culhane took to his Instagram story to share a headline about Musk’s reaction. The Sex Lives of College Girls alum simply added the following caption to his post:

Reading between the lines, Culhane’s response seems to be a bit of trolling on his part. He may not have gone into detail, but it’s easy to get the feeling that he’s not too perturbed by Musk’s reaction to his performance. On the night of the taping, the actor’s performance also generated considerable laughs from the live studio audience. As for whether Musk might feel compelled to issue a response to the comedian’s social media post, that remains to be seen.

What can probably be assumed at this point, however, is that as long as Elon Musk remains in the news, this probably won’t be the last time he’s parodied on the long-running sketch comedy show. Viewers will ultimately just have to wait and see if or how further sketches materialize and for what reason. On that note, check out Saturday Night Live when it airs on the titular night at 11:30 p.m. ET amid the 2026 TV schedule. Episodes are also available to stream with a Peacock subscription.

#3587. Wow, GTA 6 Has Some Incredible Animations

Grand Theft Auto 6GTA 6Rockstar GamesTiny Details

Grand Theft Auto 6, out now on Xbox and PS5, is a very big game. But don’t assume it’s just a blandly massive world with no tiny details to discover. Rockstar Games has packed GTA 6 with more detail than any of its previous games, including some truly impressive animations.

Let’s start with one of the earliest animations I spotted that truly made me go “Whhhooooaaa…” I parked too close to a car, and Jason was unable to fully open his door. In past GTA games, this would lead to the character teleporting out of the car or the door clipping through the other vehicle. In GTA 6, that’s not the case. Instead, Rockstar has added a dedicated animation for Jason and Lucia where they squeeze in and out of the car.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is filled with tiny animations like this that often made me shake my head and think, “I guess I get why this took so long to make.” For example, there are so many animations connected to eating and drinking in this game. I mean, you can crack open a cold one with one hand while holding and shooting an assault rifle in the other.

I also discovered that Jason and Lucia can eat a burger while holding a soda at the same time and even switch between them whenever. And when your drink is empty, you can toss it in a nearby trash can with a procedural animation that doesn’t always work. I’ve missed the trash before, and I felt like an asshole. Jason and Lucia might be murderers who rob and steal, but they aren’t litterbugs!

One animation that really caught me off-guard happened when I was testing how much damage cars in GTA 6 can take before they stop working. I found an empty parking lot, lined up my car with a nearby wall, and floored the accelerator. I expected to slam into the wall and total the front of my vehicle. Instead…

Again, GTA 6 has so many surprising animations and details. I can’t list them all here because I know I’ve not found them all yet. Maybe I never will? Regardless, I highly recommend you poke around GTA 6 and try stuff out because you’re likely to find some wild detail or tiny animation you’ve never seen before.

And for those who want to see a few more, here’s a video compilation I put together of some tiny animations I spotted while playing GTA 6 over the last few weeks. No spoilers are included in the video below.

#3586. Zendaya “Felt Overwhelmed” on the Set of ‘The Odyssey.’ Luckily, Tom Holland Came to Support Her

On the set of The Odyssey, in which Zendaya plays the goddess Athena, there were some particularly challenging days, as the actor recalled during a recent special screening attended by the cast at Los Angeles’s Academy Museum of Motion Pictures. While filming certain scenes—especially those with a crowd of extras—the 30-year-old actor felt “incredibly nervous,” she said.

How did she manage to keep the situation under control? Thank her husband, Tom Holland, whom Zendaya says went to set that day to cheer her up. Spider-Man: Brand New Day star Holland also appears in The Odyssey as Telemachus, son of Odysseus and Penelope. And although he wasn’t scheduled to work at that particular moment, he showed up anyway to support his wife.

Matt Damon’s Odysseus consults with Zendaya’s Athena in The Odyssey.

“I felt overwhelmed, to say the least,” Zendaya said at the screening, as reported by the Daily Mail, with the actor looking stunning in her cream-colored one-shoulder dress, pixie cut, and Christian Louboutin stilettos. “It was interesting because I was on a night shoot, and I remember I came in and I was like, This is like, a pinch-me moment…. I’m in front of these people who I’ve admired, but I’m just like, I don’t want to mess this up.”

While she admitted that these emotions might have worked for her character, they were not so good for her state of mind: “I was incredibly nervous, which I guess is helpful for the scene, but there’s so many other background actors as well who are performing their hearts out—so many—stunt performers who are performing and giving the most beautiful performances.”

The turning point came when Holland stepped behind the scenes to encourage her. “It helped that Tom came to set that day, and he was, like, in the corner like, ‘You got this, you’re doing good.’” It was a team effort.

Zendaya and Holland are one of Hollywood’s most admired couples, not only for their discretion (they quietly married last August 4 in Surrey) but also for the care with which they address sensitive issues, such as mental health. Even in the cult series Euphoria, Zendaya’s character, Rue, grapples with psychological issues—in addition to addiction—as a way to raise public awareness and combat the stigma that often surrounds these kinds of situations.

#3585. GTA 6 Has A Lot Of Different Bird Species, Here’s How Many

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has a lot of details and depth, including dozens of different bird species for people to find. If you're a birder, you're in for a good time.

According to The Guardian, Rockstar confirmed that there are 62 types of birds that players can spot. Players can whip out binoculars to "study" birds and animals like they could in Rockstar's last game, Red Dead Redemption II.

As PC Gamer reminds us, Florida is home to more than 500 bird types, so GTA 6 will have just a fraction of the different kinds of birds people can find in real Florida. GTA 6 was never going to replicate every single bird, of course.

Some of the birds that are found in Florida, and probably GTA 6 as well, include flamingoes, spoonbills, wood storks, egrets, kites, terns, and scrub jays. Florida is also home to bald eagles, and we'd expect them to show up in GTA 6.

Inclusive of birds, GTA 6 has more than 170 animal types, including cane toads, alligators, manatees, and rhesus macaque monkeys.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game launches at midnight local time, so it will be playable for people in New Zealand and Australia very soon. You can switch your Xbox region to New Zealand to play early, if that works.

For more on GTA 6, including preload information, preorder bonuses, and release times, check out our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

#3583. Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Breaks His Silence, Says He Would Come Back

Jensen Huang, the co-founder of Nvidia who was recently ousted as CEO after he admitted to having an affair with someone that US intelligence believes could by a spy for China, has now said he is open to returning to the company.

In his first public statement since his resignation from Nvidia, Huang told The Wall Street Journal that he is aware of the "outpouring of calls" from Nvidia employees, investors, business partners, and customers for him to come back as CEO. He would come back, if asked.

"If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO," he said.

This statement came a day after a source told CNBC that the Nvidia board is not considering bringing Huang back as CEO.

Huang released his statement on social media, saying, "Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me."

His statement added: "I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. Nvidia has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like Nvidia be possible. I love our country, and I love Nvidia."

Huang acknowledged that he "did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia" and owned up to making "serious mistakes in my personal life." He said he created problems for Nvidia's Board of Directors and he said he "deeply" regrets that. "I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation," he said.

Nvidia was the world's biggest company by market cap until the company's stock price began to crash in October, and it fell further after the controversies came to light, including multiple affairs beyond the one with the alleged spy.

To be sure, Nvidia remains a juggernaut--it's currently the No. 2 biggest company in the world, with a market cap of $3.75 trillion. Only Apple, with a market cap above $4 trillion, is bigger than Nvidia.

The New York Times and other media outlets reported that Huang had a romantic relationship with the former CEO of the AI company Megaspeed, Alice Huang (no relation). US intelligence sources claim that Alice Huang was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, though China officially denies this narrative and says it's an effort by the US to smear China.

Megaspeed, for its part, said Alice Huang left the company in 2025 and denied any wrongdoing in the Nvidia scandal.

The Nvidia controversies have led to turmoil in the stock market, in part because Nvidia is one of the "Mag 7" companies that are driving growth in the US. Some of the information coming to light suggests that Nvidia's accounting and export control compliance are not buttoned up, and this has fueled further concerns about the growth potential and returns on investment for the AI trade. Numerous other technology and AI stocks have dropped in value significantly since the Nvidia news broke.

Nvidia's interim boss is CFO Colette Kress, who is expected to lead Nvidia's earnings call today, November 17. The earnings report will be closely watched and highly scrutinized--keep checking back with GameSpot for the latest.

#3581. All The Game Awards 2026 Nominees Revealed

It's almost time for The Game Awards to kick off a night of trailers and appreciation for the 2026 gaming year, but right now, it's time to see who's in the running to earn some well-deserved kudos. The 2026 Game Awards will be livestreamed from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on December 10, and nominees for the best games across several categories have been announced.

Like previous years, the nominees have been chosen by a global jury of media publications and creator outlets--including GameSpot--and were announced through a dedicated livestream.

Leading the nominations is Grand Theft Auto 6 with eight nominations, Control Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem with six nominations each, and Phantom Blade Zero has earned an impressive five nominations. Big Walk, 007 First Light, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake have also earned plenty of nods, with four nominations each.

Game of the Year

The best of the best for 2026, the game that excelled across multiple creative and technical fields.

  • Control Resonant
  • Grand Theft Auto 6
  • Phantom Blade Zero
  • Resident Evil Requiem
  • The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

For the game that was built with an outstanding creative vision and executed it through polished direction and design.

  • Phantom Blade Zero
  • Pragmata
  • Resident Evil Requiem

Awarded to the game that not only offers the best story of the year, but also delivers its with exceptional storytelling skills.

  • Resident Evil Requiem
  • The Blood of Dawnwalker

#3580. Patriots QB Drake Maye's Wife Ann Michael Breaks Silence After Ankle Injury

New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye will “always” have a fan in wife Ann Michael Maye, even if he’s sidelined from an injury.

Ann Michael, 23, has broken her silence after Drake, 24, suffered an ankle injury during the team’s Sunday, November 15, game against the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany.

“ILY always,” she wrote via her Instagram Story on Tuesday, November 17, alongside a red heart emoji.

Ann Michael, who has been married to the NFL player since June 2025, also shared a photo of the couple kissing before Drake took the field in Europe.

Ann Michael wore a camel coat, over a navy top as she leaned in and smooched her husband. She wore a red clip in her hair as well, giving a subtle nod to the Patriots’ red, white and blue color palate.

Drake was dressed in the team’s white uniforms, holding his silver helmet in his hand as he paused for the pregame good luck kiss.

Ann Michael’s sweet message comes two days after Drake was sidelined in Sunday’s game during the first quarter after Lions’ defensive end Aidan Hutchinson sacked him.

Hutchinson, 26, was also hurt after celebrating the play, exiting the game shortly after Drake with a knee injury. (NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Hutchinson’s initial tests revealed a torn ACL in his right knee, but the Lions haven’t released an official report.)

ESPN reported on Monday, November 16, that Drake will miss “an extended period, and possibly the remainder of the season” with a suspected fractured ankle. The team hasn’t confirmed his exact injury.

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel explained on Monday’s WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show that Drake “stayed back” in Germany “out of caution” before making plans to return to the U.S. for further evaluation.

“He’ll be traveling back here shortly, but [we] just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely,” Vrabel, 51, said.

Drake, meanwhile, has yet to address his injury, but his wife has already indicated that she’ll be by his side through thick or thin.

The couple, who are childhood sweethearts, have already handled a whirlwind first year of marriage — and they aren’t showing any signs of stopping. After tying the knot in summer 2025, Drake led the Patriots to his first Super Bowl appearance in February 2026.

While the team lost to the Seattle Seahawks, Drake and Ann Michael have bonded over their new life together in Boston, far from what they both grew up knowing.

“Moving to somewhere so completely different, being away from all of our friends and family is probably the most challenging part,” Ann Michael exclusively told Us in August. “Luckily, we have great teammates and great friends here that have really made the New England area feel like home, which is great.”

She noted, “But you know, we’re both from North Carolina. Our parents live in the same neighborhood, and then we went to college in North Carolina, so we were never too far from family. That’s been the biggest adjustment.”

#3579. Glenn Close Gets Teary-Eyed as She Finally Gets Her Oscar at the Governors Awards

The day before the Governors Awards, a studio executive who had attended the past few years told me that she often found herself crying at the star-studded gala. The annual awards ceremony, held by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, is often an emotional event, with honorary Oscar statuettes bestowed on influential figures in the film industry. A tribute to Michael J. Fox in 2022 and a posthumous honor for Quincy Jones in 2024 left many guests misty-eyed.

At Sunday’s gala, that teary-eyed trend continued when Glenn Close finally got to hold her own Oscar, after eight nominations without a win. Others got emotional when Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler, the independent producers from Killer Films, were honored for their tireless work making boundary-pushing and challenging movies. And when Floyd Norman, the 91-year-old artist who was the first Black animator to join Walt Disney Animation Studios, thanked his wife and five children, the crowd cheered along with him. Even though honoree Ridley Scott couldn’t attend, he dedicated his award to his late brother Tony Scott in a video message. “It is about time we all saw him with an Academy Award in his hand,” said Matt Damon in his remarks for Scott, who has been nominated for four Oscars but has never won competitively.

The presentation of honorary Oscars is often a way to correct Academy Award history, recognizing those who have been overlooked but deserve to be honored for their lifetime of dedication to storytelling and film. The Governors Awards ceremony is also a major stop on the Oscar season campaign trail, with a room packed full of stars and filmmakers from the year’s contenders.

This year that meant a surprising number of couple contenders, including Monica Barbaro and Andrew Garfield (who both star in Artificial), Carrie Coon and Tracy Letts (The Liberation), and Zendaya and Tom Holland. Though Zendaya and Holland arrived together and walked through the Ray Dolby Ballroom as a pair, they actually sat at different tables—Zendaya at the Dune table, with Timothée Chalamet and director Denis Villeneuve, and Holland at the Odyssey table, with director Christopher Nolan. Chalamet also made a date night out of the event, bringing Kylie Jenner with him.

The room held a mix of A-list Hollywood stars, like Tom Cruise (in support of Digger), Julianne Moore (The Debut), and Charlize Theron (The Odyssey), and breakout filmmakers of the year, like Obsession’s Curry Barker, La Bola Negra’s Los Javis, and Club Kid’s Jordan Firstman.

Another breakout of the season, La Bola Negra star Guitarricadelafuente, has been busy promoting the film as both an actor and a musician, having written the original song “La Nieve.” I wondered if he was exhausted from doing double duty. “I’m not tired,” he said with a smile, raving that he had enjoyed meeting many of the other songwriters in the race this year.

All four of the presenters who handed the Oscars to the honorees are also in the Oscar race this year. Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother star Mahershala Ali honored Norman; Wild Horse Nine star John Malkovich honored his Dangerous Liaisons costar Close; Julianne Moore, teaming up with Todd Haynes, honored Vachon and Koffler; and Damon, the star of The Odyssey, honored Scott.

As Close took the stage to accept the award from Malkovich, she wiped tears away from her eyes. The star of films including Fatal Attraction, 101 Dalmatians, The Wife, Albert Nobbs, and The Big Chill spoke about being raised in a religious cult and how, in her childhood, animated films were her only escape. She also spoke about being nominated for eight Oscars over her career, insisting that it didn’t phase her not to emerge victorious. “As an outsider, I have never worried about whether I was going to win or not,” she says. “I have always felt that the great honor is to be in the room.”

She wrapped up her speech with a strong statement against AI. “The craft of acting and of great storytelling has never been more vital to the existence of our fragile, violent, but capable-of-transcendence species,” she said. “We are not machines. We are flawed. Our imperfections are our salvation.”

Vachon and Koffler have been making indie films through Killer Films since 1995, championing movies like Far From Heaven, Boys Don’t Cry, Kids, Carol, and Still Alice (which won Moore her Academy Award for lead actress). They dedicated their awards to the many people they’d worked with over the years, some of whom were in the room. “We have walked into propellers with you and what has resulted is usually a piece of work that has touched somebody. Sometimes it’s seen by millions of people and sometimes it’s seen by tens of people,” said Vachon. “But our movies came to life and made it to the screen because writers and directors trusted us with their stories and actors knew we were creating an environment that enabled them to give their best performance.”

Many of the honorees spoke about the mentors and industry giants who had helped them along the way. Close said she’d promised her World According to Garp director, George Roy Hill, that she’d thank him if she ever won an Oscar. “I never got the chance to thank the man who put me in my first movie. Now I can,” she said, holding her statuette up high. Scott, the director whose prolific career output includes Thelma & Louise, Gladiator, Black Hawk Down, Alien, Blade Runner, and The Martian, told a story in his video message about making his brother star in his very first project, the 1965 short film Boy and Bicycle. “I’m flattered and proud to accept this award, but I also accept it for Tony,” Scott said of his brother, who died in 2012. “His great work would certainly have earned this recognition.”

#3578. Xbox Game Pass Gets Even More Games In November

The second half of November is usually quiet for several reasons when it comes to new game releases–and one other big reason–but Xbox Game Pass subscribers can look forward to several new titles to close off the month--and eight games will also be leaving Game Pass on November 30.

Microsoft has announced a handful of new additions to the Game Pass library, including a kid-friendly game to kick things off and a sneak peek at some sporty fun for the first week of December. These announcements typically come in two waves, with a sneak peek split between them, so this list isn't complete yet.

The first game on the way is Paw Patrol: Dino World. Ideal for younger members of the family who definitely shouldn't be playing GTA 6 right now, this family-friendly game revolves around the PAW Patrol working together to round up lost and scared dinosaurs.

Other highlights this month include Call of the Elder Gods for a Lovecraftian puzzle-adventure, High on Life 2 joining Game Pass Premium, and Roadside Research, which is all about aliens trying to run a gas station while poorly disguised as humans.

If you're looking for action, Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 is worth checking out. All the thrill of long-distance sniping, with a surprising amount of close-quarters stealth gameplay as well. Also recommended is Motorslice, where you'll get to parkour through the ruins of a brutalist megastructure, climb massive bosses in tense fights, and hunt down living construction equipment.

Starting in December, you can get Freestyle Football 2, which is an online multiplayer soccer game built around 5v5 matches. We already have that game in the form of Rematch from Sifu developer Sloclap, but if you want a different spin on that soccer idea, take a quick look.

Xbox Game Pass November Wave 2 Games

November 17

  • Paw Patrol: Dino World (Xbox Series X|S, PC) -- Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass

November 18

  • Call of the Elder Gods (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, Handheld, and PC) -- Now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass
  • High on Life 2 (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, Handheld, and PC) -- Now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass
  • Roadside Research (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, Handheld, and PC via Game Preview -- Now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass

November 19

  • Black Jacket (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, Handheld, and PC) -- Now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass

November 24

  • Motorslice (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, Handheld, and PC) -- Now with Game Pass Premium; joining Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass
  • Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 (Cloud, Console, Handheld, and PC) -- Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass

November 27

  • Arkheron (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Game Preview) -- Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass

December 1

  • The Outlast Trials (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC) -- Game Pass Ultimate, Game Pass Premium, PC Game Pass
  • Hela: Of Mice and Magic (Cloud, Xbox Series X|S, and PC) -- Game Pass Ultimate, PC Game Pass

December 3

  • Freestyle Football 2 (Xbox Series X|S, PC)

November has been pretty good for new entries in the Game Pass library, with the start of the month bringing the dungeon-crawling roguelike deck-building game Dungeon Crawlers to more Game Pass tiers, while subscribers also got Void/Breaker, Warhammer Survivors, and John Carpenter’s Toxic Commando. Game Pass Essential saw a big influx of new games, with several Banjo-Kazooie titles joining People Can Fly’s Gears of War prequel and the beloved Viva Piñata games.

I can't remember the last time a Saturday Night Live sketch had people talking quite as much as the "Sister" sketch has. Former SNL writer and frequent host John Mulaney returned to host SNL this past weekend, and among the sketches featured was a faux medical ad for "Sister," the ultimate elder care provider for your family. The clip has sparked quite a bit of conversation after humorously raising the topic of daughters -- and in many cases, by proxy, their spouses -- being relied on more often than sons to make themselves available, and oftentimes upend their lives, to care for an aging parent. It's the rare kind of sketch that makes people laugh as much as it makes many want to cry at the truth of it.

It's been interesting to see the comments from fans across social media in response to the sketch, but I also found myself wanting to watch it again, and a few funny things caught my eye when I did.

One subtle detail that I appreciated was the fact that when Mulaney's "Brother" character texts his sister to alert her that "dad fell," we see that the previous text exchanges between the two siblings are bland Happy Birthday messages from brother.

I hate when a movie or TV series shows a text exchange on screen and it's clear there were no previous texts between two people who likely have texted in the past. Not only does the "Sister" SNL sketch avoid that bit of annoyingness, it also uses the previous texts to show us just how much distance exists between these two particular siblings. It's funny and also makes me feel bad -- kind of like the whole sketch does.

Also, I did briefly question why there wasn't a Happy Birthday text from Sister to Brother between the two he'd sent to her (marking a year passing between the two exchanges), then quickly deduced that it's likely because she called him on his birthday, instead of texting.

At the very end of the sketch, I had to pause it to read the captions. As is the case in many pharmaceutical ads, this one wraps up with a nod to the company responsible for the treatment, and then runs through a rapid but alarming list of potential side effects.

If you missed any of this, here's what it says:

This seems like a dry dig at "Brother," lest he forget that the person or people in need of care are presumably the same person/people who brought him into the world and raised him.

As for the side effects, disclaimers and warnings:

Quantities are limited. Sister may break down without warning. Offer void if sister has a good therapist.

It seems fair to warn users that the sister who's being relied on to shoulder most or all of the responsibility of care might occasionally emotionally collapse under the weight of it. And it's also fair to warn users that this "elder care system" won't work on any sister who has the psychological support to help her see through any suggestion or pressure that she should be the sole person responsible for care-giving. Quantities are limited sounds more like a mention for an HSN sale item than it does for medical treatment, but I suppose the messaging really is true for all siblings. I sure am grateful for mine!

This Saturday Night Live sketch -- written by Streeter Seidell, Mikey Day and Simon Rich -- has only been up on YouTube for a couple of days and has already amassed more than three million views. It's quickly becoming one of those sketches that makes the round and will likely be talked about and remembered for a long time. You can watch the sketch below, or check out John Mulaney's full episode of SNL with a Peacock subscription.

At present, she’s an Assistant Managing Editor who spends much of her time brainstorming and editing features, analyzing site data, working with writers and editors on content planning and the workflow, and obsessing over the best movies and TV shows. She graduated from SUNY Cortland with BA in Communication Studies and a minor in Cinema Studies. When she isn't working, she's probably thinking about work, or reading (or listening to a book), and making sure her cats are living their absolute best feline lives.

The actor playing Lucia in Grand Theft Auto 6 has been revealed, and it's Manni L. Perez, the person everyone expected it to be for a long time now. In fact, fans discovered that Perez was Lucia all the way back in 2023.

  • Best Score and Music

  • Best Performance (Manni L. Perez)

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, with a PC release reportedly on tap for early 2027.

#3574. GTA 6 Leads TGA Nominations, And Reviews Aren’t Even Live Yet

The Keighleys, or more formally, The Game Awards, are right around the corner. Ahead of its December 10 air date, host Geoff Keighley announced the nominees for the myriad categories, including Game of the Year. Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto 6 made the cut, but in an unusual circumstance, it did so before any reviews of the game have been published.

Before anyone has read any official take on GTA 6, Rockstar Games' action-adventure game has eight nominations, making it the most-nominated game at this year's The Game Awards.

On top of being spotlighted for Game of the Year, the game also has nominations for Best Art Direction, Best Audio Design, Best Game Direction, Best Action/Adventure, Best Narrative, Best Performance (for Manni L. Perez's portrayal of Lucia), and Best Score, bringing the crime sim's total nominations to eight.

We already knew GTA 6 would be eligible for this year's ceremony. After all, per the TGA FAQ, the cutoff date for eligibility is November 20, one day after the game comes out. With a "jury of over 100 global media and influencer outlets" selecting the nominees, and many of these folks likely having plenty of hands-on time with Rockstar Games' latest release, it isn't much of a shocker to see GTA 6 at the top spot. Still, it is a little awkward that it has so many nominations before its release that may reveal what to expect from the critical reception..

Maybe it shouldn't be too surprising or weird, though. After all, the game isn't officially out yet, and it's already sold approximately 16 million copies and generated nearly $2 billion in revenue. Maybe that expensive sick day caused by the GTA Flu won't be so expensive.

#3573. Lil’ Kim Takes The Spotlight—With A Symphony

When you hear the name Lil’ Kim, a variety of images come to mind. She’s forever known as the force of nature from Brooklyn who turned the music industry on its head when she entered the scene, and her bodacious lyrics and unique fashion sense have kept her as a source of inspiration on your favorite designer’s mood board ever since. On November 18 and 19, to celebrate the music that cemented her icon status, Lil’ Kim will perform in front of a symphony orchestra at the Kings Theatre in Brooklyn, not far from her humble beginnings.

Today she’s less interested in being in the spotlight and more focused on raising her 12-year-old daughter, Royal Reign. In between practices for her performances, Lil’ Kim spoke with Vanity Fair to reflect on her career, how she spends her days, and her standout looks.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Vanity Fair: What do you remember about putting your debut album, Hard Core, together?

Lil’ Kim: I remember Biggie and Un [Lance Rivera], who was the label owner that we had. I watched Un build a record label called Undeas, which [stood] for “Un ideas,” and then he finally sold it to Atlantic Records. At the time, we didn’t know the process, but we became Undeas-Atlantic. I remember Biggie having the idea of how he wanted my album to be red, and he explained it to me and Un. I was able to write according to how his idea was to present me, because when they met me, I was who I was—in high heels, jeans, motorcycle jackets, and furs at 13.

Portrait of members of R&B group 112 and rappers Notorious BIG and Lil’ Kim circa 1996

That’s incredible. It sounds like your fashion-icon status started very early. Was there anyone that you looked to back then? What inspired you to dress that way?

My mom was a big inspiration to me when it came to fashion, and so I looked to her for a lot of things. I used to wear her mink coat. She used to wear big sunglasses with her fur coats, with the diamonds and jewelry. She was always taking vacations and I would see her pack her stuff, and she would always have the cutest outfits. They were all matchy-matchy. It’s funny because she would have her outfit to go play tennis in and her outfit would match her tennis racket. So when I bought my big house, I bought a Chanel tennis outfit and I bought the racket to match it, because of my mom.

I love that. Do you keep up with tennis or specifically the ladies in tennis?

No, I haven’t in a while, but, of course, you know, Serena and Venus were like my heroes.

Well, maybe we need to see you on the court one day.

I know. I’m pretty sure I’m rusty, but I like to get out there, though. I used to beat my cousin’s butt back then.

How did the symphony performances come about?

My agents called me and they’re like, “Kim, what do you think?” And I was like, “That’s a freaking awesome idea.” I love performing with bands. And so I imagine that it could be very similar, if not very close. And I thought this could be something really different for me. Sometimes I even listen to classical music. I don’t have to know who the artist is, but I just put on a station and let it flow.

Do you have a favorite song from Hard Core?

I love “Queen Bitch”; it’s my favorite song. It’s still my favorite to perform. And “Crush on You.”

Salma Hayek, Donatella Versace, Pamela Anderson, and Lil’ Kim at Versace’s spring/summer 2001 fashion show

When it comes to fashion, you’re obviously on everyone’s mood board, from stylists to designers, so how important was fashion for you as part of the Lil’ Kim persona?

I just was being myself, honestly. When I first met Biggie, I was coming from my after-school job at Bloomingdale’s. I was probably 13 or 14 at the time, and they would let the teenagers work there.

But I had on a motorcycle jacket and high heels. And one of my best friends told Biggie, “You know, my girl can rap,” because we knew he was rapping around the way. And he was like, “I heard you can rap.” And I just laughed. He was like, “Yeah, see, I knew you didn’t know how to rap.” He was very condescending. He knew how to get you to do what you wanted to do, because I was really shy.

And then I started rapping, and he was blown away because I had on high heels. No one had ever seen someone just bust a rap in high heels. When Biggie, Un, and Jacob York started really talking to me, they didn’t want to change me because that was just what they were so blown away about. That was just who I was.

Do you think people ever misunderstood the way you presented yourself?

To be honest, I never really felt misunderstood by my hardcore fans—the kids my age and the younger kids, they totally got it. I think that’s why I had such a cult following and there was such pandemonium about me when I came out. They understood me. I think it was the older people and the politicians, those are the people who I think misunderstood me.

What did you think of the midterm elections and all of the women who broke barriers in the Senate and gubernatorial offices?

I’m going to be honest with you, I stay away from politics.

Are you keeping up with all of the changes within fashion today? When I listen to your music, you’ve mentioned so many designers and houses, and since then the creative directors have changed. Are you following all of the changes within fashion and seeing how you’re still a part of the conversation?

That’s what I’m trying to say. As a fashion icon, if you really her, and I’m considering myself really her, that’s never gonna change. That’s never going to change. I might put on a fur coat that my stylist or myself will get asked about, because I style myself a lot. And I was styling myself then.

Lil’ Kim and daughter, Royal Reign, on June 16, 2016, in New York City

Extremely rewarding. My daughter’s with me all the time. This world is so cruel and so evil; it’s so different. She’s my safe haven. I feel the extra need to keep her safe.

What does a regular day look like for you?

Lately, I’ve just been really getting into myself. I get up and go have a little spa day. I might take my daughter to go do whatever she wants.

Singer Mary J. Blige with Diana Ross and Lil’ Kim at the 1999 MTV Video Music Awards on September 9, 1999

How do you feel that we’re still talking about your MTV VMAs look in 1999?

I think it’s iconic and I love it. I love when they bring that up, because it was a fun day and it was so good to see people’s faces when they saw my outfit.

Are there any other looks that don’t get as much love as you wish that they did?

I don’t know, because most of the looks that I love, they get the love. There’s a look when I was on the cover of Nylon magazine and I had the teddy bear dress on; that’s one of my favorite looks. The Louis Vuitton look is one of my favorite looks; I love that look. A lot of the Chanel looks and the Versace and the Chanel in the hair.

I have no idea if this is the case of some reviewers just not being in the target audience of The Hunger Games’ latest prequel Sunrise on the Reaping or if some people who have liked the other movies found this one less moving. But looking at reviews this morning after Sunrise purple carpet photos dropped, I realized not everyone felt the way I did about the 2026 movie release.

I agree with reviews on one big point: The adaptation is faithful to Suzanne Collins’ source material, which is a pretty bleak book with a bittersweet ending in the same way the third Hunger Games book is. That’s down to several scenes I personally wanted to see play out on the big screen.

Discussing Film made a big point to call out the adaptations “faithful” take on the source material. The outlet’s Yasmine Kandil wrote:

That being said, Sunrise on the Reaping remains exceedingly faithful to the novel’s sequence of events, perhaps more so than any of its predecessors, and often down to the most minute details.

In fact, I saw that word peppered in and out of reviews. If you liked the book, you should like this movie. Or as Gizmodo's Germain Lussier more than adequately puts it, if you are a fan of this franchise, you'll dig this. It's a "love letter" to fans.

Sunrise on the Reaping, is a love letter to The Hunger Games, filled with connections, explanations, and moments designed to provide maximum delight to fans of the series. It isn’t concerned with setting up the world or reexplaining the stakes. It says, 'This is the sixth movie. If you’re watching this without context, well, that’s on you.'

Still, when it comes to SOME of these reviews, I feel like I watched a completely different movie.

At Indiewire, the grade was a C- (with a bright spot in Jesse Plemons’ performance as Plutarch), and this comment from Ryan Lattanzio is really sticking with me after perusing reviews.

Sunrise on the Reaping is a dreary slog, another death-march “They Shoot Horses, Don’t They?” riff with a pretty Gen Z cast, and one that mistakes new layers of darkness (and trauma!) for the sort of profundity that its filmmakers hope will burnish a creatively withering property.

The Guardian was equally unenthusiastic about the movie, and had seemingly a lot of fun lambasting it, calling it “overwrought” and “boring,” and even making fun of the flick’s name. ( I think Peter Bradshaw’s review highlights my earlier point, that this movie isn’t for every demographic.)

Here is yet another iteration of the utterly exhausted, unbearably extended and now surreally boring Hunger Games franchise, based on the YA bestsellers by Suzanne Collins. This one has another of the series’ convoluted faux-mythic subtitles: Sunrise on the Reaping. What, “harvest dawn” not old-timey enough?

These aren’t the only two bad reviews, they are just among the more brutal and trending. (Though it's worth pointing out plenty of outlets, like THR, Time Out and more gave the film positive reviews, and it is at the time of this writing, trending positively on review aggregators.)

Honestly, is Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping perfect? No. Mckenna Grace and Jesse Plemons are standouts, and Elle Fanning and Joseph Zada do fine jobs, but I’m not bringing up Oscars here. I also think because the movie is so long, some of the emotional deaths in the arena are blunted, and I wish we had more time with characters like Maysilee, Wiress, Beetee and Ampert.

Regardless, this movie made me feel a lot of feelings about humanity, and what humans are willing to endure. Haymitch’s story ties in so hard with Katness,’ and the end cap OG Hunger Games scene where she was able to do what he could not was both hopeful and sad at the same time. This movie emotionally wrecked me. I cried multiple times. If you are a fan of the franchise at all, you should see it on the big screen. It’s proven to be a franchise with staying power and (hopefully) more stories to tell.

Jessica Rawden is Managing Editor at CinemaBlend. She’s been kicking out news stories since 2007 and joined the full-time staff in 2014. She oversees news content, hiring and training for the site, and her areas of expertise include theme parks, rom-coms, Hallmark (particularly Christmas movie season), reality TV, celebrity interviews and primetime. She loves a good animated movie. Jessica has a Masters in Library Science degree from Indiana University, and used to be found behind a reference desk most definitely not shushing people. She now uses those skills in researching and tracking down information in very different ways.

#3571. What Does It Take For World Of Warcraft To Be Nominated At The Game Awards?

The nominees for 2026's The Game Awards have been revealed, and just like every year before it, there is a glaring omission in the Best Ongoing Game Category: World of Warcraft.

This year's nominees are Arc Raiders, Fortnite, No Man's Sky, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, and Final Fantasy 14 Online. Of particular note is Square Enix's MMORPG, which has been nominated in the category every year since 2021. Developer Blizzard's MMO, on the other hand, is nowhere to be seen. 

WoW is among the most popular live-service games in industry history and has been for 22 years. Blizzard releases new expansions for its MMORPG every other year like clockwork and has done so for over two decades. It reintroduced the old-school version of the MMO, WoW Classic, in 2019 to huge acclaim from the game's passionate community.

In the years that followed, it continued to add new expansions to the modern version of WoW, adding highly requested features like account-wide unlocks and new endgame solo content. For WoW Classic, it re-released past expansions, added official servers and support for a permadeath mode popular among the game's community, and ran experimental seasons that added new content to the classic version of the game. Taken all together, the various versions of WoW have millions of players.

Earlier this year, Blizzard released Midnight, the latest expansion for modern WoW that added player housing to the MMO for the first time. A few weeks ago, it released WoW: Forever, the third major version of the MMO. Built on the bones of WoW Classic, Forever is intended to be an ongoing game that will add new content and changes to the old-school version of WoW, existing alongside the modern game. Forever was the biggest launch in WoW history in terms of concurrent players, Blizzard said.

Yet, since 2017, WoW has never even been nominated in Best Ongoing Game, a category that serves to put a spotlight on titles that continue to receive new content and evolve the experience over time--something Blizzard wrote the book on with WoW.

WoW being omitted this year in particular is more baffling than any time before, as Blizzard not only released a brand-new expansion, but also an entirely new version of the game that players have dreamed about for years. On the other hand, Final Fantasy 14's new expansion, Evercold, doesn't release until 2027, even if the game has received significant content updates over the course of the year. 

Even other Blizzard games have been nominated in this category multiple times over the years. Overwatch won Best Ongoing Game in 2017 and was nominated again in 2018. Diablo 4 earned a nomination in 2024 with the release of its first expansion, Vessel of Hatred. 

Meanwhile, it seems like nothing WoW does is enough to warrant attention. There is, of course, a simple answer to why this seems to be the case--nobody, or at least very few, on the The Game Awards voting jury plays, or keeps up to date, with WoW.

That's a shame, because if there was any year where WoW deserved to be nominated, it's this year. Forever is the culmination of an entire community's dream of having an ongoing, new version of classic WoW, and Midnight continues the philosophy of player-friendly changes first added in 2024's The War Within expansion. There are now more ways to play WoW than ever before, each receiving unprecedented support and updates. In fact, players in the modern version of WoW have been complaining that there's perhaps too much to do and that content updates are maybe too frequent. 

This is all to say that it feels like WoW deserves just a little recognition. It's been running for over two decades at this point, and in that time has in many ways defined what an "ongoing game" is and can be. 2026 has been a banner year for WoW, and its future is looking brighter than ever. It deserved a moment in the spotlight. Maybe next year (though I wouldn't bet on it).

On the big day, Ann Michael attended the ceremony with Drake when it was revealed he’d be joining the Patriots.

Ann Michael attended one of Drake’s first NFL games. “Just the beginning,” she captioned an Instagram pic of the couple on the sidelines.

The couple got engaged when Drake dropped to one knee in a gorgeous oceanfront proposal.

“Love doing life with you,” Drake shared via Instagram. “Can’t wait to marry you!”

Drake and Ann Michael didn’t waste much time tying the knot, getting hitched six months after their engagement.

“Happy birthday to my better half, my best friend, and lucky enough to call you my wife❤️ I love you,” the NFL player wrote via Instagram on August 11 while celebrating Ann Michael’s birthday.

A few weeks later on August 30, Ann Michael toasted Drake’s birthday, writing via social media, “Happy birthday to my forever person❤️ I love you more than you know and am beyond lucky to be your wife! So thankful I get to do this life with you🥰.”

During the 2025-2026 NFL season Ann Michael started to go viral on TikTok for her cooking skills — especially when her videos featured her husband or were about feeding the football player.

A November 5 video of Ann Michael’s spiced apple cider donut loaf was viewed more than 175,000 times within one week and received more than 550 comments.

“Thank you for taking care of Drake Maye, First Lady of New England,” one fan wrote.

The following month, Ann Michael hosted a “Merry Bakemas” baking countdown where she cooked a sweet treat or bread ahead of the holidays. Drake was a frequent taste tester and guest in the TikTok series.

Drake gave fans a glimpse at his home life with Ann Michael during a January 21 press conference, revealing they are both pretty competitive.

“She started playing mahjong,” Drake said. “I haven’t gotten into that. Something like that. Playing Battleship or cards or anything that goes off of me playing her.”

He noted that the couple picked up playing tennis in the offseason and love to make a game out of it. “She’ll try anything we can compete in. She’s a great athlete,” Drake added.

Later that month, Ann Michael was by Drake’s side when he led the Patriots to a victory over the Denver Broncos in the AFC Championship Game, securing a spot in Super Bowl LX — the first of his career.

While most fans were thrilled to see the Pats make their way back to the big game, others couldn’t stop talking about Drake’s body language towards Ann Michael after the January 25 victory.

“Why does he always seem so standoffish around her? She was so excited,” one user wrote in the comments section after the NFL shared a video of Ann Michael congratulating Drake after the game where he appeared to be looking everywhere but at his wife who is trying to hug him.
